questions.stem: If at 10k per kg, 1000 kg of yam were purchased and at 5k per kg, 1,500 kg were purchased, the resultant point elasticity of demand is
If, as the price of a commodity rises, the quantity demanded of the commodity remains the same, then the demand for the commodity is
questions.explanation: Quantity unchanged whatever the price means elasticity is zero: perfectly inelastic.

questions.stem: Which of the following factors is an important determinant of the magnitude of price elasticity of demand?
questions.explanation: Durability affects how easily purchases can be postponed and so how price-elastic demand is; the other options affect supply.

questions.topic: Factors of Production and their Theories
questions.stem: The marginal theory of distribution makes an assertion that the price of any factor depends upon its marginal
questions.explanation: Marginal productivity theory: a factor is paid according to its marginal (revenue) productivity.

questions.stem: In order to increase its profit margin, the monopolist can manipulate
questions.explanation: A monopolist can fix price or output but not both, since demand determines the other.

questions.stem: For a purely competitive industry, a fundamental requirement of the demand curve faced by individual firms is that it should be
questions.explanation: Each competitive firm is a price-taker facing a horizontal (perfectly elastic) demand curve.

questions.stem: The merging of firms engaged in different stages of production and marketing is called
questions.explanation: Vertical integration combines firms at different stages of the same production chain.

questions.stem: Which of the following is an important function of the retailer?
options: Breaks bulk and sells products in small units
Generates demand for products through advertisement
questions.explanation: Retailers break bulk and sell in small quantities to final consumers.

questions.stem: The table gives the various levels of output (Q) and the corresponding total cost of production (TC) and total revenue (TR) for a firm: Q (ton) 400, 500, 600, 700, 800, 900, 1000; TC (N) 16000, 18000, 19800, 21000, 24000, 31500, 4000; TR (N) 2000, 22500, 24000, 24500, 24500, 18000, 15000. Which output level Q results in maximum profit?
questions.explanation: Profit = TR - TC: at 500 it is 22500 - 18000 = 4500, higher than at 600 (4200) or 700 (3500).

questions.stem: One of the purposes of advertisement in marketing is to
options: Change the quality of the product
Raise the quantity of the product demanded as its price falls
Shift the demand curve for the product to the right
questions.explanation: Advertising aims to increase demand at every price, shifting the demand curve rightwards.

questions.stem: The size of a business unit tends to be small if the activity
options: Involves the provision of direct services
questions.explanation: Direct personal services (e.g. barbing, tailoring) favour small firms.

questions.stem: Which type of business organization has the attribute of effectively combining management with control?
questions.explanation: In a sole proprietorship the owner both controls and manages the business.

questions.stem: The co-operative as a form of business organization differs from partnership by having
options: Several sources of capital for business financing
Ability to issue preferred stocks to members
Entrenched democratic control in the conduct of business
Established rules and regulations governing the activities of its members
questions.explanation: Co-operatives are run democratically on one member, one vote.

questions.stem: The type of business finance that entitles the holder to a fixed rate of dividend is
questions.explanation: Preference shares carry a fixed rate of dividend; debentures earn interest, not dividend.

questions.stem: Which of the business organizations listed below is characterized by limited authority and liability of the individual owners?
questions.explanation: Shareholders of a joint stock company have limited liability and limited individual authority.

questions.stem: A company is said to be highly geared if the
options: Value of fixed interest loans is high compared with share capital
Value of share capital is high compared with fixed interest loans
questions.explanation: High gearing means a large proportion of fixed-interest debt relative to equity.

questions.stem: Industries that can be randomly located are characterized by
options: Relatively low transport cost for both raw materials and output and factor mobility
Relatively heavy transport cost for raw material or output
questions.explanation: Footloose industries have low transport costs and mobile inputs, so they can locate almost anywhere.

questions.stem: The term ‘double coincidence of wants’ is usually associated with a
questions.explanation: Barter requires each party to want what the other has: a double coincidence of wants.

questions.stem: A major factor affecting the value of money is the
questions.explanation: The value (purchasing power) of money varies inversely with the general price level.

questions.stem: Cost-push inflation is caused by
questions.explanation: Cost-push inflation results from rising costs of production such as wages and raw material prices.

questions.stem: The stock exchange market is where
options: The federal government trades on treasury bills
Existing bonds and stocks are traded
New stocks and shares are bought or sold
questions.explanation: The stock exchange is chiefly a secondary market for existing securities.

questions.stem: Commercial bank reserves at the Central Bank have the effect of
questions.explanation: Required reserves limit banks' lending capacity and so control credit and money supply.

questions.stem: A tax is defined as regressive if
options: The proportion of income paid as tax increases as the income level increases
All income groups pay the same percentage of their income as taxes
The proportion of income taken by the tax falls as income increases
The proportion of income taken by the tax is a fixed nominal amount of income for all income groups
questions.explanation: A regressive tax takes a smaller proportion of income as income rises.

questions.stem: Government intervention in an economy is often justified on the ground that
options: Wants are unlimited while resources are scarce
Productivity is higher in the public than in the private sector
Free market may not work or produce desired results
Opportunity cost of government expenditure is zero
questions.explanation: Market failure (the free market not producing desired results) justifies government intervention.

questions.stem: The three major groups of government revenue are
options: Investment income, direct tax and indirect tax
Import duties, excise tax and export duties
Company tax, personal income tax and import duties
Company tax, import duties and excise tax
questions.explanation: Government revenue broadly comes from direct taxes, indirect taxes and non-tax income such as investment income.

questions.stem: The main objectives of public expenditure do NOT include
options: Achievement of a more equitable income distribution
Meeting the social needs of the people
questions.explanation: Public expenditure aims at stabilization, equity and social welfare, not profit maximization.

questions.stem: A perfect example of a public good is
questions.explanation: Defence is non-rival and non-excludable and is provided by government: a pure public good.

questions.stem: A balanced budget is defined as a condition of
options: Equality of aggregate demand and aggregate supply
Equality of planned receipts and planned expenditure
Equality of planned exports and planned imports
questions.explanation: A balanced budget means planned revenue equals planned expenditure.

questions.stem: Item (million naira): visible exports 55.54; visible imports 53.32; invisible exports 30.56; invisible imports 28.70; balance 4.08. The amount N4.08 million, shown as balance in the table, represents
questions.explanation: (55.54 - 53.32) + (30.56 - 28.70) = 4.08: visible plus invisible balance is the current account balance.

questions.stem: By using exchange controls, a country tries to eliminate a balance of payments deficit by
options: Limiting her imports to its currency value of exports
Reducing the nation’s domestic price level
Limiting her exports to its currency value of imports
questions.explanation: Exchange control rations foreign exchange so imports do not exceed export earnings.

questions.stem: The law of comparative advantage states that a country should specialize in the production of a commodity
options: For which local demand is greatest
In which its opportunity cost is lower than that of the trade partner
For which foreign demand is greatest
For which there is abundant supply of raw materials
questions.explanation: Comparative advantage rests on lower opportunity cost relative to the trading partner.

questions.stem: International and inter-regional trade differ primarily because
options: Comparative advantage is relevant to the former but not the latter
There are different resource supplies among countries of the world
questions.explanation: International trade crosses national boundaries (with different currencies and regulations); inter-regional trade does not.

questions.stem: Optimum population is the population level at which
options: Death rate is at a minimum
Per capita income is at maximum
Death rate is equal to birth rate
questions.explanation: Optimum population is the size that maximizes output (income) per head given resources.

questions.stem: The group of people engaged in banking or insurance services by occupational distribution are classified as
questions.explanation: Banking and insurance are services, i.e. tertiary production.

questions.stem: The difference between gross national product and net national product is equal to
questions.explanation: NNP = GNP - depreciation (capital consumption).

questions.stem: The value of the total output produced within Nigeria by all residents (citizens and non-citizens) is referred to as the
questions.explanation: GDP measures output produced within the country's borders regardless of nationality.

questions.stem: The multiplier is defined as
options: The ratio of the change in income to the change in investment
The change in investment divided by the change in income
questions.explanation: k = change in income / change in investment (= 1/MPS = 1/(1 - MPC)).

questions.stem: If C stands for consumption expenditure, I for investment, X for exports, and M for imports, then national income is
questions.explanation: Expenditure on domestic output = C + I + (X - M) in this model without government.

questions.stem: A sustained increase in the per capita income of a country over a period of time is called
questions.explanation: Economic growth is a sustained rise in real output/income per head.

questions.stem: The primary goal of development planning in Nigeria is to
options: Achieve a rapid increase in the welfare and standard of living of Nigerians
Increase the level of gross domestic product
questions.explanation: Development plans ultimately aim at raising the welfare and living standard of the people.

questions.stem: If one orange costs 20k and one kilogram of beef costs N10.00, the opportunity cost of one kilogram of beef is
questions.explanation: N10.00 = 1000k, which would buy 1000/20 = 50 oranges.

questions.stem: In economic life, choice among alternatives depends on the
options: Scale of preference of the decision maker
questions.explanation: Faced with scarcity, a decision maker chooses according to his scale of preference.

questions.stem: One of the major advantages of specialization is that
options: The worker becomes a tender of machines
It causes more employment of labour
Less machinery is required for production
The worker wastes less time between operations
questions.explanation: A specialised worker does not move between tasks, saving time between operations.

questions.topic: Factors of Production and their Theories
questions.stem: Which of the following rewards is associated with entrepreneurship as a factor of production?
questions.explanation: Profit is the reward of the entrepreneur.

questions.stem: A firm achieves least-cost in production by substituting factors until
options: The ratio of their marginal-physical-products equals the ratio of their prices
Their marginal-physical-products are each equal to their factor prices
Their marginal-physical-products are each equal to zero
questions.explanation: Least cost requires MPa/Pa = MPb/Pb, i.e. the ratio of marginal products equals the ratio of factor prices.

questions.stem: Economies of scale operate only when
options: Marginal cost is falling with input
Average cost is falling with output
Variable cost is less than fixed cost
questions.explanation: Economies of scale exist when long-run average cost falls as output expands.

questions.stem: At the point of profit maximization by a firm, marginal cost is
questions.explanation: Profit is maximized where MC = MR with MC cutting MR from below, i.e. MC rising.

questions.stem: A situation in which all inputs are doubled and output also doubles is known as
questions.explanation: Output rising in the same proportion as all inputs is constant returns to scale.

questions.stem: The law of diminishing marginal utility indicates that if a consumer increases his consumption of a commodity continuously his
options: Marginal utility may rise even though his total utility is falling
Marginal utility may fall even though his total utility may be rising
questions.explanation: The law states that each additional unit consumed yields less extra satisfaction, so marginal utility falls.

questions.stem: Technical progress that leads to reduction in costs results in
options: An increase in equilibrium price and quantity
A decrease in equilibrium price and quantity
An increase in equilibrium price and decrease in equilibrium quantity
A decrease in equilibrium price and increase in equilibrium quantity
questions.explanation: Lower costs shift supply to the right, lowering price and raising quantity.

questions.stem: If an increase in income induces a reduction in the demand for beans, beans can be referred to as
questions.explanation: A good whose demand falls as income rises is an inferior good.

questions.stem: The demand for a product is said to be price inelastic if
options: The price elasticity of demand is less than one
The price elasticity of demand is greater than one
A reduction in price results in an increase in quantity demanded
An increase in price results in a decrease in the quantity demanded
questions.explanation: Inelastic demand has a coefficient of price elasticity less than one.

questions.stem: An imperfect market in which there is only one buyer of a commodity is
questions.explanation: A single buyer is a monopsony.

questions.stem: The tailoring service is competitive partly because it consists of a large number of
questions.explanation: Tailoring is dominated by many small-scale firms, which makes it competitive.

questions.stem: Which of the following is applicable to a monopolistic firm operating at the output where marginal cost equals marginal revenue?
options: Cost of production is at a minimum
The plant is of optimum size
Average variable cost is at a minimum
questions.explanation: A monopolist faces a downward-sloping demand curve, so price (AR) exceeds MR at the profit-maximizing output.

questions.stem: In the distribution channels for goods and services, the middleman’s mark-up margin provides a rough measure for the
options: Effectiveness of government control over economy’s marketing channels
Extent of exploitation of the final consumer
questions.explanation: The mark-up is the middleman's reward for the services and risks of distribution.

questions.stem: A major difference between a state-owned enterprise and private enterprise is that the former
options: Is not expected to cover its cost of production while the latter is
Is not always expected to maximize profits while the latter is
Has shareholders while the latter does not
Has a board of directors while the latter does not
questions.explanation: Public enterprises pursue social goals as well as profit, while private firms aim at profit maximization.

questions.stem: Divorce of ownership from control is a characteristic of
questions.explanation: In a (public) limited liability company the shareholders own it while directors/managers control it.

questions.stem: Capital provided by individuals to the firm by purchasing stocks is called
questions.explanation: Funds raised by selling shares (stocks) are equity capital.

questions.stem: Which of the following factors is the most important in siting a petro-chemical plant?
options: Nearness to the source of raw materials
Nearness to the source of power
questions.explanation: Petro-chemical plants are located near their bulky raw material (crude oil/gas).

questions.stem: Which of the following will be the effect of allowing only economic factors to dictate the location of industries in Nigeria?
options: A more even development of the different parts of the country will be assured
There will be an unbalanced spread in the distribution of industries
The less developed parts of the country will be able to attract more industries
Only the government will be able to finance the establishment of industries
questions.explanation: Purely economic location concentrates industries in favoured areas, causing uneven distribution.

questions.stem: Which of the following is likely to be inflationary?
questions.explanation: Wage increases raise costs and spending, causing cost-push pressure; the others are deflationary.

questions.stem: The basic purpose of imposing legal reserve requirements on commercial banks is to
options: Assure the profitability of commercial banks
Provide a device through which credit creation by banks can be controlled
Provide a proper ratio between earning and non-bank assets
Provide the Central Bank with working capital
questions.explanation: Reserve requirements limit the credit banks can create.

questions.stem: Which of the following is a liability of a commercial bank?
options: Loans made by the bank to individuals
Loans made by the bank to other banks
questions.explanation: Customers' deposits are owed by the bank, so they are liabilities; loans and bonds are assets.

questions.stem: A tax on a commodity whose supply is perfectly inelastic is
options: Divided in the ratio 60:40 between the consumer and the supplier
Divided half-and-half between the producer and the consumer
questions.explanation: With perfectly inelastic supply, the supplier cannot reduce quantity and so bears the whole tax.

questions.stem: Under a system of freely floating exchange rate, an increase in the international value of a country’s currency will cause
options: Gold to flow into that country
Its currency to be in surplus
questions.explanation: Appreciation makes imports cheaper and exports dearer, so imports rise.

questions.stem: Balance of trade is the difference between
options: Exports and imports of goods and services
questions.explanation: Balance of trade is the visible balance: exports minus imports of goods.

questions.stem: Which of the following is likely to reduce a surplus in the balance of payments of a country?
questions.explanation: Appreciation makes exports dearer and imports cheaper, reducing a surplus.

questions.stem: Which of the following is a tariff?
options: Limit on the amount of goods which can be imported
Government payment to domestic producers for exports
questions.explanation: A tariff is a tax/duty on imports; a quantity limit is a quota.

questions.stem: Import duties will increase total expenditure on imports if the demand for imports is
questions.explanation: If demand is inelastic, quantity falls proportionately less than price rises, so total spending rises.

questions.topic: Factors of Production and their Theories
questions.stem: Which of the following is likely to hinder labour mobility in Nigeria?
questions.explanation: Lack of information about jobs elsewhere hinders movement of labour; the others encourage it.

questions.stem: If birth rate is constant and death rate declines, population
questions.explanation: Natural increase = birth rate - death rate; a falling death rate raises population growth.

questions.stem: Disposable income is an income which
options: Is available for consumption and savings
Is payable to the disabled members of the community
Accrues to the environmental sanitation authorities for refuse disposal
questions.explanation: Disposable income is income after tax, available for consumption and saving.

questions.stem: In equilibrium, injections are equal to
questions.explanation: National income is in equilibrium when injections (I + G + X) equal withdrawals (S + T + M).

questions.stem: Social overhead capital refers to
questions.explanation: Social overhead capital is infrastructure such as roads, power and water supply.

questions.stem: The most common index used for measuring development is
questions.explanation: Per capita income is the most widely used single indicator of development.

questions.stem: Agriculture is central to Nigeria’s economic development because
options: Nigeria’s comparative advantage lies mainly in agro-allied industries
Agriculture is the largest employer of labour
Agriculture accounts for an insignificant domestic product
Nigeria earns limitless foreign exchange from agriculture
questions.explanation: Agriculture employs the majority of Nigeria's labour force.

questions.stem: In a market economy, the questions of what, how and for whom to produce are solved by the
questions.explanation: In a market (free enterprise) economy the basic economic questions are answered by the forces of demand and supply, i.e. the price mechanism.

questions.stem: Economic goods are termed scarce goods when they are
options: not available in sufficient quantities to satisfy all wants for them
not produced in sufficient quantities to satisfy the effective demand for them
of primary importance in satisfying the needs of a society
questions.explanation: Scarcity means the quantity available is not enough to satisfy all the wants for the good.

questions.stem: A school girl who needs a book and a mirror, each costing five naira, decides to purchase the book instead of the mirror since she cannot pay for the two at the same time. Determine the real cost of her book.
options: The five naira she spent on the book
questions.explanation: Real (opportunity) cost is the alternative forgone, which is the mirror.

questions.stem: Macroeconomics is a study of economic science from the point of view of
questions.explanation: Macroeconomics studies the economy as a whole, i.e. aggregates.

questions.stem: If units of a variable factor are increasingly added to a fixed factor and the marginal physical product keeps increasing, production is said to be taking place under condition of
options: increasing returns to the variable factor
constant returns to the variable factor
questions.explanation: With one factor fixed, a rising marginal physical product of the variable factor means increasing returns to that variable factor (returns to scale require all factors to vary).

questions.stem: At any given level of output, the total cost of a firm equals the
options: marginal cost plus the average cost
fixed costs less its variable cost
average cost multiplied by its output
economic costs multiplied by variable costs
questions.explanation: AC = TC/Q, so TC = AC x Q.

questions.stem: At any given level of output, a firm's total variable cost equals
options: total cost less total fixed cost
average variable cost and marginal variable cost
questions.explanation: TC = TFC + TVC, so TVC = TC - TFC.

questions.stem: Consider a diagram where XYZ represents the average cost curve of a firm. XY shows that as output increases the average cost declines. However, this decline cannot continue indefinitely because of
questions.explanation: Economies of scale (managerial, indivisibilities, risk pooling) make AC fall, but they are limited by the size (extent) of the market.

questions.stem: If the price of a ball point pen falls from N1.00 to N0.60 and the quantity demanded increases from 200 to 300, the point elasticity of demand is equal to
questions.explanation: %change in Qd = 100/200 = 50%; %change in P = 0.40/1.00 = 40%; elasticity = 50/40 = 1.25.

questions.stem: If a society is operating on the production possibility curve, this implies that the resources are
questions.explanation: Points on the PPC represent full and efficient use of resources; points inside it show under-utilisation.

questions.stem: A market is in disequilibrium if
options: the quantity purchased is greater than the quantity sold
the quantity sold differs from the quantity purchased
at a lower price, a larger quantity is sold
the quantity demanded differs from the quantity supplied
questions.explanation: Equilibrium occurs where quantity demanded equals quantity supplied; any difference is disequilibrium.

questions.stem: The cross-elasticity of demand between complementary goods is
questions.explanation: For complements, a rise in the price of one reduces demand for the other, so cross-elasticity is negative.

questions.stem: Resources are efficiently allocated when production takes place at that output where price equals
questions.explanation: Allocative efficiency requires P = MC.

questions.stem: Comparison of the price and output decisions of a perfectly competitive firm with those of a monopolist shows that the
options: monopolist charges a lower price than the perfect competitor
perfect competitor charges a lower price and produces a larger output than the monopolist
perfect competitor produces a smaller output than the monopolist
monopolist charges a lower price and produces a larger output than the perfect competitor
questions.explanation: A monopolist restricts output and charges a higher price than a perfectly competitive industry.

questions.stem: In a perfectly competitive market, the firm is in long-run equilibrium at the output where
questions.explanation: In the long run P = MR = MC = minimum AC, so the firm produces at the lowest point of its average cost curve.

questions.stem: Which of the following statements must hold if price discrimination is to be possible?
options: Elasticities in the various markets must not differ
The markets must not be separated but integrated
The markets should be separable but there should be no resale
questions.explanation: Price discrimination requires separable markets (with differing elasticities) and no resale between them.

questions.stem: The ordinary partner in a partnership
options: takes no active part in management of the business
has limited liability in case of business failure
has unlimited liability in case of business failure
cannot be sued personally on matters relating to the business
questions.explanation: An ordinary (general) partner bears unlimited liability for the debts of the firm.

questions.stem: A possible factor which limits the extent of growth of a firm is the
options: unwillingness to share ownership and control
questions.explanation: Owners who will not admit new partners or shareholders cannot raise the extra capital needed to grow.

questions.stem: One of the most outstanding disadvantages of co-operative societies as business organizations is that
options: true spirit of co-operation is marred by delegated authority
membership interest is centered on sharing of essential commodities
questions.explanation: Co-operatives rely on members' small contributions and so are usually poorly financed.

questions.stem: A disadvantage of a joint-stock company is
questions.explanation: Shares can be bought by outsiders, so original owners may lose controlling interest; limited liability and continuity are advantages.

questions.stem: A characteristic of a debenture is that
options: its yield is based on profits
its yield is a fixed rate of interest
there is a voting when interest is paid
questions.explanation: A debenture is a loan to the company carrying a fixed rate of interest.

questions.stem: Industries tend to be located closer to market centres than to the sources of major raw materials if the
options: products are relatively cheap to transport to market centres
products are relatively more expensive to transport than the major raw materials
raw materials can also be imported
questions.explanation: When finished products cost more to transport than the raw materials, firms minimise costs by locating near the market.

questions.stem: One disadvantage of trade by barter is that
options: people are happier when they exchange the same quantities of goods through the medium of money rather than by barter
the person wishing to buy good X may not have good Y which is what the other person wants
one person must always be cheated when trade takes place by barter
it increases the initial cost of producing goods
questions.explanation: Barter requires a double coincidence of wants.

questions.stem: One of the functions of Development Banks is to
options: mint money for the development of the economy
provide short-term loans to commercial banks
provide medium and long-term finance for development of the banking system
provide medium and long-term finance for the development of the economy
questions.explanation: Development banks provide medium- and long-term funds for economic (industrial/agricultural) development.

questions.stem: To perform its function as a store of wealth and standard for deferred payment, money must be
options: spent more on capital goods than on consumer goods
questions.explanation: Money can store value and settle future debts only if its value is stable.

questions.stem: Fiduciary issue is that part of
options: the issue of notes backed entirely by gold
a country's currency which is not negotiable
the issue of notes not backed by gold
questions.explanation: The fiduciary issue is the part of the note issue not backed by gold, resting only on confidence (government securities).

questions.stem: An effect of inflation is that it
options: favours debtors at the expense of creditors
increases the real income of salary earners
increases the value of a country's exports
questions.explanation: Inflation reduces the real value of money repaid, benefiting debtors at creditors' expense.

questions.stem: Banks aid economic expansion and development by
options: being very strict in lending policies
questions.explanation: Banks mobilise savings and lend them for investment.

questions.topic: Factors of Production and their Theories
questions.stem: The term 'Stock of Capital' means
options: amount of money necessary to start a business
total amount receivable by all factors of production
amount of equipment, plant and inventory existing at a time
total amount available for economic development
questions.explanation: The capital stock is the quantity of man-made producer goods (plant, equipment, inventories) existing at a point in time.

questions.stem: A tax that takes an increasing fraction of income as income goes down is called
questions.explanation: A regressive tax takes a larger proportion of lower incomes.

questions.stem: Budget deficit is the amount by which
questions.explanation: A budget deficit occurs when total government expenditure exceeds total revenue.

questions.stem: The average tax rate is defined as
options: total tax rate less the marginal tax rate
the tax rate which applies to additional value of income
the ratio of total taxes paid to total income
marginal tax rate for being progressive
questions.explanation: Average tax rate = total tax paid / total income; option B describes the marginal rate.

questions.stem: Personal distribution of income implies
options: the way income is distributed among specific households or spending units
the distribution of income according to basic resource classes
dividing income between personal taxes, consumption expenditures and savings
questions.explanation: Personal distribution is about how income is shared among households; B describes functional distribution.

questions.stem: One of the advantages of international trade is that it
options: promotes self-reliance and satisfaction with only what can be produced internally
questions.explanation: Specialisation according to comparative advantage raises total world output.

questions.stem: There is an improvement in the terms of trade of a country if
options: a large quantity of exports is given up to obtain a unit of imports
the volume of exports is greater than the volume of imports
a smaller quantity of exports is given up to obtain a unit of imports
the value of exports is greater than the value of imports
questions.explanation: Terms of trade improve when each unit of exports buys more imports, i.e. fewer exports are given up per unit of imports.

questions.stem: Under flexible exchange rates, a deficit could be corrected by
questions.explanation: A deficit makes the home currency depreciate (other currencies appreciate), making exports cheaper and imports dearer, which corrects the deficit.

questions.stem: The higher the dependency ratio the
options: larger the proportion of the employed relative to the unemployed
smaller the proportion of the active labour force relative to the inactive
smaller the number of the non-working age groups relative to the active labour force
questions.explanation: Dependency ratio = dependants / working population, so a higher ratio means fewer active workers relative to dependants.

questions.stem: The age distribution of a country's population is of economic importance because it affects the
questions.explanation: The proportions of young, working-age and old people determine the goods and services demanded and government spending needs.

questions.stem: It is important to measure the National Income of a country because
options: it is a major determinant of the standard of living
it reveals hazards of development like pollution and congestion
it reveals the distribution of the citizens' savings in foreign banks
its size determines the extent of political stability
questions.explanation: National income estimates are used to assess and compare living standards.

questions.stem: The Gross Domestic Product is defined as the total value of
options: all final goods and services produced in a country during the year
all assets of a country in a particular year
exports net of total value of imports
questions.explanation: GDP is the total value of final goods and services produced within a country in a year.

questions.stem: Stage of product / value of input / sale value of output: Maize farmer - nil / N10.00; Flour miller - N10.00 / N12.00; Baker - N12.00 / N15.00; Shop keeper - N15.00 / N20.00. The value of total output in the economy using the value added approach is
questions.explanation: Value added = 10 + (12-10) + (15-12) + (20-15) = N20, equal to the value of the final product.

questions.stem: If W stands for wages/salaries, P for profit, R for interest and Z for rent on land and real estate, then national income is
questions.explanation: By the income approach national income is the sum of all factor incomes: wages + profit + interest + rent.

questions.stem: In the national income and product accounts, double counting is avoided if
options: only intermediate and final goods are counted
the value of all goods and services are added together
questions.explanation: Counting only final goods (or only value added) avoids counting intermediate goods twice.

questions.stem: A major obstacle to economic development is
questions.explanation: Low agricultural productivity keeps incomes and savings low in developing economies, hindering development.

questions.stem: Which of the following situations can give rise to economic problems?
options: Limited means available for satisfying wants
questions.explanation: Economic problems arise from scarcity - the limited means available to satisfy wants - which forces choice.

questions.stem: Scale of preference refers to
options: list of goods and services in order of priority
budget preparation without paying due regard to priority
questions.explanation: A scale of preference is a list of wants arranged in order of importance.

questions.stem: For an economy which last year produced only two commodities X and Y, the real cost of the quantity of X which it produced can be measured by the
options: amount of X it could not produce
total amount of Y it could have produced
extra amount of Y it could have produced
questions.explanation: The real (opportunity) cost of X is the additional Y that was forgone by producing X.

questions.stem: Which of the following is applicable in a wholly capitalist economy?
options: There is government intervention in price determination
Households cannot freely decide what to spend on goods and services
questions.explanation: In a pure capitalist economy resources are allocated by the price mechanism with consumer sovereignty and no government price control.

questions.stem: Age group (years) / Distribution (%): Above 60 - 30; 15 - 60 - 45; 0 - 14 - 25. The estimated dependency ratio of the population distribution shown above is
questions.explanation: Dependants = 30 + 25 = 55%; working age = 45%; 55 : 45 = 11 : 9.

questions.stem: Population (million) / Food production (million tonnes): 50 - 220; 70 - 210; 90 - 225; 100 - 275. In the data above, what is the optimum population in million?
questions.explanation: Food per head: 220/50 = 4.4, 210/70 = 3.0, 225/90 = 2.5, 275/100 = 2.75; output per head is highest at 50 million, the optimum.

questions.stem: The major objective of the current campaign for family planning in Nigeria is to
options: limit the number of women a man can marry
keep the population growth rate constant
raise the standard of living of the population
questions.explanation: Family planning aims to slow population growth so that living standards can rise.

questions.stem: The migration of young people from rural to urban areas in Nigeria should help to raise the
options: standard of living in the urban areas
total productivity of labour in the rural areas
marginal productivity of labour in the rural areas
marginal productivity of labour in the urban areas
questions.explanation: Removing surplus labour from the land raises the marginal product of the workers who remain in rural areas.

questions.stem: By definition, variable cost (VC) is related to total cost (TC) and fixed cost (FC) by the equation
questions.explanation: TC = FC + VC, so VC = TC - FC.

questions.stem: The higher the price of capital relative to the price of labour, the more production techniques should be
questions.explanation: A cost-minimising firm substitutes the relatively cheaper factor, here labour.

questions.stem: Use the following production and cost data of a profit-maximizing firm. Calculate the marginal physical product of the last unit of input.
questions.explanation: MPP of the 5th unit = 22 - 20 = 2.

questions.stem: The U-shape of the long-run average cost curve can be explained by the
options: concepts of economies and diseconomies of scale
questions.explanation: Long-run AC first falls because of economies of scale and later rises because of diseconomies of scale.

questions.stem: Quantity of singlets / short-run total costs (N): 0 - 1,000; 10 - 1,200; 20 - 1,400; 30 - 1,600; 40 - 1,800. The short-run total costs for different levels of output for a firm producing singlets are shown above. Calculate the variable cost per unit at an output of 20.
questions.explanation: Fixed cost = TC at zero output = N1,000; VC at 20 = 1,400 - 1,000 = N400; AVC = 400/20 = N20.

questions.stem: If demand is relatively inelastic and sellers are able to raise the price of their commodity, then there will be a
options: fall in both quantity demanded and total revenue
fall in the quantity demanded and a rise in total revenue
fall in the quantity demanded and a rise in marginal revenue
rise in both the quantity demanded and the marginal revenue
questions.explanation: With inelastic demand, quantity falls proportionately less than price rises, so total revenue increases.

questions.stem: A firm with marginal cost equal to its marginal revenue will produce the equilibrium output if it is in
questions.explanation: MC = MR is the profit-maximising (equilibrium) condition in every market structure.

questions.stem: An important function of the retailer is to
options: break bulk and sell products in small units
generate demand for products through advertisement
questions.explanation: Retailers break bulk and sell in the small quantities consumers want.

questions.stem: The main handicap of sole proprietorship is
questions.explanation: A sole trader depends on personal savings and small loans, so capital is usually inadequate.

questions.stem: The type of business organization mostly used for producing public goods in Nigeria is
questions.explanation: Public utilities are provided mainly through government-owned statutory corporations.

questions.stem: The main reason for the current programme of privatization and commercialization of public enterprises in Nigeria is to
options: encourage efficiency in the performance of such enterprises
reduce the number of public enterprises
raise the prices of goods and services produced by the enterprises
questions.explanation: Privatization and commercialization were introduced mainly to make public enterprises efficient and profitable.

questions.stem: Farmers' income may fall if they produce more cash crops for export because
options: the price of the crops will rise
questions.explanation: With inelastic demand, a larger supply lowers price proportionately more, so total revenue falls.

questions.stem: Under the Nigerian structural adjustment programme, the marketing of agricultural commodities in Nigeria has been placed under
questions.explanation: SAP (1986) abolished the commodity boards and liberalised marketing of agricultural produce to private operators.

questions.stem: The primary barrier to land reform in developing countries is the
options: realization that output levels might fall
fear that peasants will be cut off from credits
general contentment with the present arrangement
questions.explanation: Powerful landowners usually resist redistribution of land.

questions.stem: The consumer-goods industry is predominant in the industrial sector of the Nigerian economy because of
options: availability of market and most of the raw materials required
availability of the necessary machinery required
relatively lower cost of production of such goods
questions.explanation: Consumer-goods industries thrive where there is a large ready market and accessible raw materials.

questions.topic: Natural Resources and the Nigerian Economy
questions.stem: A significant effect of the growth of the oil sector in Nigeria has been to
options: diminish the percentage contribution of the agricultural sector to GNP
slow down the pace of industrialization and urbanization
retard the rate of economic growth
questions.explanation: The oil boom reduced agriculture's share of GNP as oil came to dominate output and exports.

questions.topic: Natural Resources and the Nigerian Economy
questions.stem: Because most of her crude oil is exported, the foreign exchange earnings and the forward linkage effects Nigeria realizes from her oil production are
questions.explanation: Exporting crude earns much foreign exchange, but little local refining/processing means weak forward linkages.

questions.stem: Which of the following is NOT directly concerned with dealings in treasury bills?
questions.explanation: Treasury bills are money-market instruments handled by the CBN, banks and discount houses; the Stock Exchange deals in long-term securities.

questions.stem: Monetization refers to the ratio of
options: money in circulation to total income
questions.explanation: The degree of monetization is the proportion of all transactions carried out with money.

questions.stem: The best way to reduce the supply of money in the economy is to
options: increase the number of bank notes and cheques produced
questions.explanation: Raising the liquidity ratio reduces banks' ability to create credit, cutting money supply.

questions.stem: The total amount of money in circulation includes cash
options: and current account balances owned by the non-bank public
owned by banks and the non-bank public
and current account balances owned by banks and the non-bank public
owned by banks, the government and the non-bank public
questions.explanation: Narrow money supply is currency held by the non-bank public plus their demand (current account) deposits.

questions.stem: To reduce the high rate of inflation in the economy, Government should
options: increase taxes and have a budget surplus
increase taxes and have a budget deficit
decrease taxes and have budget deficits
decrease taxes and have a balanced budget
questions.explanation: Contractionary fiscal policy - higher taxes and a budget surplus - reduces aggregate demand and inflation.

questions.stem: When interest rates are high and still rising, the least-cost method used by public limited companies to obtain additional funds for their operations is by
options: obtaining long-term loans from merchant banks
obtaining short-term loans from commercial banks
selling floating-rate debenture stocks to the general public
selling new ordinary shares to the general public
questions.explanation: Ordinary shares carry no fixed interest charge, so they avoid the high and rising cost of borrowing.

questions.stem: The objective of public finance is to promote
options: full employment, national income and price stability
government revenue drive and expenditure to as high a level as possible
the expansion of government social services
government revenue drive and minimise government expenditure
questions.explanation: Public finance aims at macroeconomic goals such as full employment, growth of income and price stability.

questions.stem: An account from which allocations are made to the three tiers of government in Nigeria is called the
questions.explanation: Federally collected revenue is paid into the Federation Account and shared among federal, state and local governments.

questions.stem: Use the information: Year 1 - GNP at current prices N20,000m, population 20 million; Year 2 - GNP at current prices N27,000m, population 24 million. What is the percentage increase in GNP between year 1 and year 2?

In national income accounting, aggregate saving in any year is defined as
options: all disposable income not spent on consumption
all savings deposits in all banks during the year
all savings and time deposits in all banks during the year
the value of inventory change for the year
questions.explanation: Saving = disposable income - consumption.

questions.stem: Which of the following combinations is a veritable set of development indicators?
options: Growth of government expenditure and imports
Growth of population and national income
High fertility, literacy and school enrolment rates
Low infant mortality and high per capita income and literacy rate
questions.explanation: Development is indicated by welfare measures such as low infant mortality, high per capita income and high literacy.

questions.stem: If an economy grows at an annual rate of 5% of which 3% is deemed to be due to improvement in the productivity of labour and capital combined, the remaining 2% is generally attributed to
questions.explanation: Growth not explained by factor inputs (the residual) is attributed to technical progress.

questions.stem: If a country has a balance of payments crisis, which of the following measures can best bring about an improvement in the short run?
options: Large-scale export of locally made goods
Repayment of debt to her creditors
questions.explanation: Increasing exports brings in foreign exchange and improves the balance of payments.

questions.stem: The terms of trade of a country is defined as
options: (Index of import prices / Index of export prices) x 100
(Index of exportables / Index of importables) x 100
(Index of visible imports / Index of visible exports) x 100
(Index of export prices / Index of import prices) x 100
questions.explanation: Terms of trade = export price index / import price index x 100.

questions.stem: When a foreigner on a visit to Nigeria pays for hotel accommodation and meals with some foreign currency, the amount paid should be recorded in Nigeria's balance of payments as an item of
questions.explanation: Services sold to foreigners (tourism) are invisible exports.

questions.stem: The Nigerian Trust Fund is managed on behalf of Nigeria by the
questions.explanation: The Nigeria Trust Fund (1976) is administered by the African Development Bank.

questions.stem: One of the gains by member states of the Economic Community of West African States is
questions.explanation: Removing trade barriers within ECOWAS creates trade among members.

questions.stem: It is impossible to satisfy all human wants because
options: areas of fertile land are very limited
oceans and seas limit land space for farming
questions.explanation: Wants are unlimited while the resources for satisfying them are limited (scarcity).

questions.stem: A diagram showing the maximum possible combinations of commodities X and Y produced in Nigeria is called the
questions.explanation: The production possibility curve shows the maximum combinations of two goods obtainable with given resources and technology.

questions.stem: The main function of the price system is to
options: distribute resources equally among competing ends
ensure efficient allocation of resources in the economic system
questions.explanation: The price mechanism allocates scarce resources efficiently among competing uses.

questions.stem: A system in which the means of production is held in trust for the people by government is known as a
questions.explanation: Under socialism the state owns the means of production on behalf of the people.

questions.stem: The working population refers to
options: a population where the average age is falling
the population within the 0-14 age bracket
the economically active segment of the population
questions.explanation: The working population is the economically active part of the population.

questions.stem: Which of the following factors is NOT responsible for the rural/urban drift in Nigeria?
options: Declining fertility of rural farm lands
Higher living standards in urban areas
questions.explanation: Rural electrification improves rural amenities and so discourages, rather than causes, rural-urban drift.

questions.stem: An accurate census is important to a country because it helps
options: to ensure equitable population redistribution relative to natural resources
in deciding on the creation of more local governments
in providing a sound basis for formulating development policy
questions.explanation: Reliable population data are essential for economic planning and policy formulation.

questions.stem: If 502.75 million tonnes of grains are consumed annually by a population of 88.5 million people, the per capita grains consumption will be
questions.explanation: 502.75 / 88.5 = 5.68 tonnes per person.

questions.stem: In the theory of production and cost, the average total cost of a firm is minimized when the marginal cost curve cuts the average total cost at its
questions.explanation: MC cuts ATC from below at the minimum point of ATC.

questions.stem: A firm faces diminishing returns when its
questions.explanation: The law of diminishing returns sets in when the marginal product of the variable factor starts to fall.

questions.topic: Factors of Production and their Theories
questions.stem: If profit maximization is assumed to be the objective of a business enterprise, labour must be paid a wage rate equal to the
options: marginal revenue product of labour in the enterprise
questions.explanation: A profit-maximising firm hires labour until the wage equals the marginal revenue product of labour.

questions.stem: If the equilibrium price of a certain commodity is N120.00 and the government fixes its price at N110.00, the supply will be
options: the same as the equilibrium supply
a determinant of the market forces of equilibrium
questions.explanation: A maximum price below equilibrium reduces the quantity producers are willing to supply.

questions.stem: If the price elasticity of demand for a certain commodity is less than unity, then
options: an increase in the price of the commodity will raise the total revenue of the producer
an increase in price leaves the total revenue unchanged
a decrease in price raises the total revenue of the supplier
a decrease in price leaves the total revenue constant
questions.explanation: With inelastic demand, price and total revenue move in the same direction.

questions.stem: At equilibrium one of the distinctive features of monopoly compared with perfect competition is that in the former
options: price is always equal to marginal cost
supply is always equal to demand
price is always higher than marginal cost
there are always many buyers and many sellers
questions.explanation: A monopolist sets MR = MC with P > MR, so price exceeds marginal cost; under perfect competition P = MC.

questions.stem: Use the table: Output (units) / Total revenue (N): 1 - 20; 2 - 38; 3 - 54; 4 - 68; 5 - 80. Given an output of 3 units, the average revenue is
Use the table: Output (units) / Total revenue (N): 1 - 20; 2 - 38; 3 - 54; 4 - 68; 5 - 80. Determine the marginal revenue if the total revenue is N80.00.
questions.explanation: TR of N80 is at 5 units; MR = 80 - 68 = N12.

questions.stem: Production is said to be completed when
options: goods and services reach the consumers
prices of goods or services are determined
goods are sold to the wholesaler
questions.explanation: In economics production is complete only when goods and services reach the final consumer.

questions.stem: A debenture share entitles its holder to
options: participate in the annual general meeting of the company
receive a fixed interest on sums invested
have a representative on the Board of Directors
questions.explanation: Debenture holders are creditors entitled to fixed interest, not dividends or votes.

questions.stem: A public limited liability company is different from a private limited company because it
options: is registered with the Registrar of companies
can raise capital of any size by way of loans
can sell shares on the Stock Exchange
questions.explanation: Only a public company can offer its shares to the public through the Stock Exchange.

questions.stem: A modern corporation is owned by
questions.explanation: Ordinary shareholders are the owners (equity holders) of a company.

questions.stem: Wheat grows best in
questions.explanation: Wheat is a temperate crop.

questions.stem: On the basis of the contribution to employment, the most important economic sector in West Africa is
questions.explanation: Agriculture employs the majority of the labour force in West Africa.

questions.stem: The most popularly adopted industrialization strategy in West Africa is
questions.explanation: West African countries largely adopted import-substitution industrialization.

questions.stem: One of the most important factors that should be considered in the location of an industry is
questions.explanation: Location decisions depend chiefly on access to raw materials (inputs) and markets.

questions.stem: Since the mid-1980s, the most disturbing development in the industrial sector in Nigeria is
questions.explanation: With SAP-era import and forex constraints, Nigerian factories operated far below installed capacity.

questions.stem: The money market is a financial market that specializes in the provision of
questions.explanation: The money market deals in short-term funds; the capital market in long-term funds.

questions.stem: Which of the following programmes in the monetary sector is aimed at enhancing the banking habit of the rural areas?
options: The deregulation of the banking system
The increase in the number of merchant banks
questions.explanation: Community banks (1990) were set up to provide banking services in rural communities.

questions.stem: Economic development is distinguishable from economic growth because the former
options: is not concerned with growth parameters
also includes an efficient distribution of economic growth
is an increase in the production of goods and services
questions.explanation: Development includes growth plus improvements in distribution and welfare; option D describes growth.

questions.stem: Which of the following can be considered as being outside the objectives of public finance?
options: The allocation of resources to various sectors of the economy
The objectives of even distribution of income and wealth
questions.explanation: Allocation, distribution and stabilization are the objectives of public finance; deregulation is not.

questions.topic: Natural Resources and the Nigerian Economy
questions.stem: The joint ventures operating in the Nigerian oil industry are between
questions.explanation: The oil joint ventures are partnerships between NNPC and the oil-producing companies (Shell, Mobil, Chevron, etc.).

questions.stem: Which of the following are the major disadvantages of the direct system of taxation? I. Disincentive to hard work II. Difficulties in assessment and collection III. Imperfections in tax assessment
questions.explanation: Direct taxes may discourage effort and are difficult and imperfect to assess and collect, making evasion easy.

questions.stem: According to the income approach to national income measurement, the national income of a country is equal to
options: the value of all output produced in the country over the relevant period of time at market prices
the value of output at factor cost
questions.explanation: The income approach sums factor incomes, which equals the value of output at factor cost.

questions.stem: The best index for international comparison of standards of living is the
questions.explanation: Per capita income adjusts national income for population size, allowing comparison between countries.

questions.stem: The G.D.P. of Nigeria will be greater than her G.N.P. if
options: the value of goods and services to Nigeria is greater than the value of those from Nigeria
government expenditures are greater than the foreign aid received
the value of goods and services produced by Nigerian businesses abroad is less than that of foreign businesses in Nigeria
questions.explanation: GNP = GDP + net factor income from abroad; when foreigners earn more in Nigeria than Nigerians earn abroad, GDP exceeds GNP.

questions.stem: Below equilibrium, the gap between aggregate demand and the full employment level of income is called the
questions.explanation: When aggregate demand falls short of the full-employment level of income, the shortfall is a deflationary gap.

questions.stem: Which of the following are the advantages of Nigeria's membership of ECOWAS? I. A greater opportunity for trade according to comparative cost advantage II. A larger market for industries producing under conditions of decreasing cost III. Competition for home-based monopoly firms
questions.explanation: Economic integration widens trade on comparative advantage, enlarges markets for scale economies and exposes domestic monopolies to competition.

questions.stem: Comparative advantage implies that a country will specialize in producing the commodity
options: for which output per worker is lower than in other countries
for which output per worker is the same as those of other countries
questions.explanation: A country has a comparative advantage in the good it produces at the lowest opportunity cost.

questions.stem: Devaluation is effective when
options: demand for imports is price inelastic
demand for exports is price elastic
questions.explanation: Devaluation cheapens exports; it improves the balance of payments only if demand for exports (and imports) is elastic.

questions.stem: From which of the following does Nigeria derive trade concessions?
questions.explanation: Under the Lome Convention the EEC granted ACP countries such as Nigeria trade concessions.

questions.stem: Tariffs on imports are meant to
options: prevent a country from becoming a dumping ground for foreign goods
increase the level of external dependency
questions.explanation: Import tariffs protect domestic industries, e.g. against dumping.

questions.stem: The International Bank for Reconstruction and Development is important to developing countries because it
options: gives loans to member countries for legal proceedings
offers grants and aid for defence
offers loans to member countries for socio-economic activities
offers grants and aid to finance luxury projects
questions.explanation: The IBRD (World Bank) lends to member countries for development projects.

questions.stem: The basic economic problems of the society include
options: what to produce, how and for whom
scarcity, when to produce and how
scarcity, for whom to produce and where
questions.explanation: The basic economic problems are what to produce, how to produce and for whom to produce.

questions.stem: Opportunity cost is an economic concept which describes the
options: monetary equivalent of the utility of a commodity
amount of time or money invested on a commodity
sacrifice made for the satisfaction of a want
cost of retaining an optimum level of production of commodities
questions.explanation: Opportunity cost is the alternative sacrificed in satisfying a want.

questions.stem: If the marginal propensity to consume is 0.80 and the investment expenditure changes from N100 million to N140 million in a given economy, find the level of equilibrium in the given economy, using the formula K = 1/(1 - MPC) (K = Multiplier; MPC = Marginal Propensity to Consume)
questions.explanation: K = 1/(1 - 0.8) = 5; change in investment = N40m; change in equilibrium income = 5 x 40 = N200 million.

questions.stem: The circular flow of income defines the
options: relationship between ends and means in the economic system
allocation of income to various members of the household
flow of goods, services and money among the various macro-sectors of the economy
questions.explanation: The circular flow traces flows of goods, services and money between households, firms and other sectors.

questions.stem: The necessity of choice is due to the fact that
questions.explanation: Because wants are insatiable while resources are scarce, choice is necessary.

questions.stem: In a mixed economy, decisions to produce are taken by
options: men and women acting in their own best interest
the government acting in the interest of the country
the market women, the labour unions and the employers association
private individuals, organizations and the government
questions.explanation: A mixed economy combines private enterprise and government in production decisions.

questions.stem: Every economy requires an accurate census because it assists in
options: providing a sound framework for policy formulation
stimulating economic activities in the national economy
questions.explanation: Accurate population data provide a basis for planning and policy formulation.

questions.stem: The population of country X in 1990 was 35 million. The births were 450,000 while it recorded 210,000 deaths. If in the same year its immigrants were 20,000 and 10,000 of its citizens left the country, calculate the total population of the country at the end of 1990.
If the actual population in a country is less than the optimum population, then
options: it is desirable to have a large population
it is necessary to have an improved technology to sustain the population
it is desirable to have a smaller population
the available resources are inadequate to sustain the population
questions.explanation: Under-population means output per head would rise with more people, so a larger population is desirable.

questions.stem: When the Total Product (TP) is at its maximum point, the Marginal Product (MP) and the Average Product (AP) respectively are

questions.stem: In the long run, all production factors are
questions.explanation: The long run is a period long enough for all factors to be varied.

questions.stem: A firm determines its profits when it studies its
options: average cost relative to price in the market
questions.explanation: Profit per unit is price (AR) minus average cost, so profit is found by comparing AC with market price.

questions.topic: Factors of Production and their Theories
questions.stem: An increase in the supply of labour in a factory while other things remain equal will lead to
options: an increase in the wage rate and an increase in the number of people employed
a decrease in the wage rate and a decrease in employment
an increase in the wage rate and decrease in employment
a decrease in the wage rate and an increase in employment
questions.explanation: A rightward shift of labour supply lowers the equilibrium wage and raises employment.

questions.stem: Price (N) / Quantity demanded / Quantity supplied: 10 - 50 - 450; 20 - 150 - 350; 30 - 250 - 250; 40 - 350 - 150; 50 - 450 - 50. What is the equilibrium quantity?

questions.stem: Above the equilibrium point, a further rise in price tends to

questions.stem: Elasticity of demand is an effective tool in the hands of a producer in that it enables him to
options: raise his profits and lower his cost
set his price to maximize his profit
questions.explanation: Knowing how quantity responds to price lets the producer set the price that maximises revenue/profit.

questions.stem: Cross elasticity of demand can be mathematically expressed as the

percentage change in quantity demanded / percentage change in price
percentage change in quantity demanded of commodity X / percentage change in price of commodity Y
percentage change in quantity demanded / percentage change in income
questions.explanation: Cross elasticity = %change in Qd of X / %change in price of Y.

questions.stem: The basic idea behind brand differentiation under an imperfect market arrangement is to
options: create demand for the particular product
enable the product to penetrate the market
enable the product to compete with others
questions.explanation: Product differentiation aims to create a separate (loyal) demand for the firm's own brand.

questions.stem: In the long run, a firm in a perfectly competitive market will make
questions.explanation: Free entry and exit eliminate abnormal profits, leaving only normal profit in the long run.

questions.stem: Output restriction, fixing of prices and creating obstacles to free entry into the market are features of
questions.explanation: A pure monopolist restricts output, sets price and is protected by barriers to entry.

questions.stem: In the event of liquidation of a private limited liability company, the shareholders' liability is limited to their total
questions.explanation: Limited liability means shareholders can lose only the capital they invested in the company.

questions.stem: The major factor that causes fluctuations in the supply of agricultural produce is
questions.explanation: Agricultural output depends heavily on weather, so weather variation causes supply fluctuations.

questions.stem: The system of agricultural practice which involves hunting, gathering and growing of food crops for family consumption only is described as
questions.explanation: Producing only for the family's own consumption is subsistence farming.

questions.stem: What is the term used to describe a policy aimed at promoting the local production of goods which are usually imported?
questions.explanation: Import substitution replaces imports with locally produced goods.

questions.stem: Labour-intensive strategy of industrialization emphasizes the use of
questions.explanation: Labour-intensive production relies mainly on human (manual) labour rather than machines.

questions.topic: Natural Resources and the Nigerian Economy
questions.stem: Petroleum is the mainstay of the Nigerian economy because it is the
options: greatest contributor to the growth of agriculture
source of high income for its workers
questions.explanation: Oil provides the bulk of Nigeria's foreign exchange earnings and government revenue.

questions.stem: An increase in both the legal reserve ratio and the discount rate has the effect of
options: increasing the quantity of money in circulation
decreasing the quantity of money in circulation
questions.explanation: Higher reserve requirements and a higher discount rate restrict bank lending, reducing the money supply.

questions.stem: Inflation in the Nigerian economy may be fueled by an increase in
options: the dollar price of crude oil
questions.explanation: Increased government expenditure raises aggregate demand and can fuel inflation.

questions.stem: Gresham's law in economics shows that
options: good money drives out bad money
bad money drives out good money
the value of money varies inversely with the price level
gold must be available to maintain the value of paper money
questions.explanation: Gresham's law: bad money drives good money out of circulation.

questions.stem: Monetary policy aimed at reducing demand-pull inflation in the country may be carried out through
options: increase in taxation of private companies, public corporations and private individuals
increase in cash reserve ratio of commercial banks and the sales of government securities
decrease in government expenditure on education
direct price control in the market place
questions.explanation: Raising the cash reserve ratio and open-market sales of securities are monetary tools that reduce money supply; A and C are fiscal measures.

questions.stem: A progressive tax structure is designed to
options: take more from the income of the poor
take more from the income of the rich
take equal proportion of income from both the rich and the poor
reduce the problems emanating from tax imposition
questions.explanation: A progressive tax takes a higher proportion of higher incomes.

questions.stem: Taxes and government expenditures are instruments of
questions.explanation: Fiscal policy uses taxation and government spending.

questions.stem: The national income of a country indicates that the gross national income was N17,700 million and gross domestic product was N16,800 million. The difference of N900 million represents
questions.explanation: GNP - GDP = net factor income from abroad.

questions.stem: If national income rises by 6% and population rises by 3%, per capita income will
questions.explanation: Per capita income growth is approximately 6% - 3% = 3%.

questions.stem: One of the ways by which the government can speed up economic development is through the
options: increase in consumption pattern of the people
encouragement of savings, investment and equitable distribution of goods and services
increase in the rate of population growth so as to ensure that the country has a large labour force
encouragement of importation of raw materials to produce consumer goods
questions.explanation: Savings and investment raise capital formation, and equitable distribution improves welfare, speeding development.

questions.stem: A sustained increase in the production of goods and services in a country is called economic
questions.explanation: Economic growth is a sustained increase in a country's output of goods and services.

questions.stem: One of the techniques for rectifying a deficit balance of payments is
questions.explanation: Devaluation makes exports cheaper and imports dearer, helping to correct a deficit.

questions.stem: The main objective of the Economic Community of West African States is to
options: establish a West African Development Bank
introduce a common currency for the sub-region
promote the free movement of persons, goods and services within the sub-region
questions.explanation: ECOWAS aims at economic integration through free movement of persons, goods and services.

questions.stem: In international trade, shipping and other freight charges are treated as
questions.explanation: Shipping and freight are services, i.e. invisible items in the current account.

questions.stem: A situation in which a commodity is sold abroad below its cost of production in the home country is known as
questions.explanation: Selling abroad below home cost/price is dumping.

questions.stem: The borrowing rights of a member country of the International Monetary Fund are determined by
options: the seriousness of the country's economic problems
the size of its gold reserve
questions.explanation: A member's access to IMF resources is determined by its quota.

questions.stem: The ultimate objective of economics is to
options: make effort to understand how the economy works
make the best use of scarce resources
organize production at the lowest cost
decide under what circumstances in the economy
questions.explanation: Economics exists because resources are scarce relative to wants, so its end goal is the best use of those scarce resources.

questions.stem: A student in Obu'pu Secondary School discovers that he simultaneously needs a biro, an exercise book, an eraser and a ruler, but that he can purchase only one of these items. What is the first thing he is expected to do?
options: Check how much money he has
Find out which is the cheapest of the items
Draw up a scale of preference
Weigh the opportunity cost of each item against the others
questions.explanation: Faced with several wants and limited means, a rational consumer first ranks the wants in order of importance, i.e. draws up a scale of preference.

questions.stem: What to produce in any society is determined by the
options: expenditure of the people on different commodities
supply and demand in the factor markets
questions.explanation: Consumers' spending ('voting with their naira') signals which goods are wanted, so it determines what is produced.

questions.stem: The active intervention of the central authorities in the management of a country's economy rests upon the
options: failure of the market forces to produce satisfactory results
superiority of the centrally planned economy over the private enterprise economy
result-oriented nature of the private enterprise economy
cost-minimization strategy of a mixed economy
questions.explanation: Government intervention is justified by market failure, i.e. the inability of market forces alone to produce satisfactory outcomes.

questions.stem: An ageing population is a population
options: in which the number of old persons is increasing
that is dominated by very old people
questions.explanation: An ageing population is one in which the proportion/number of old people is rising.

questions.stem: The population of Ohaha L.G.A. was 480,000 in December 1980 out of which 60% were females. If within one year no births were recorded, but 5% of the males died, what will be the population of the L.G.A. in December 1981?

questions.topic: Factors of Production and their Theories
questions.stem: What is meant by labour supply?
options: Number of people in working population
Number of men and hours they work
Number of hours during which the middle aged persons work
Number of work force multiplied by the hours they work
questions.explanation: Labour supply is the total number of workers available multiplied by the hours they are willing to work.

questions.stem: The advantages which firms obtain directly from expanding their operations are referred to as
questions.explanation: Cost advantages arising from a firm's own expansion are internal economies of scale.

questions.topic: Factors of Production and their Theories
questions.stem: The factor of production that has the highest degree of mobility is
questions.explanation: The entrepreneur, whose organising skill can be applied in any industry or place, is regarded as the most mobile factor; land is immobile.

questions.topic: Factors of Production and their Theories
questions.stem: Any payment to a factor of production in excess of what is necessary to keep that factor in its present employment is known as
questions.explanation: Economic rent is earnings above transfer earnings.
