questions.explanation: MP of 2nd worker = 46 - 24 = 22; AP at 5 workers = 95/5 = 19.

questions.stem: Given that TC = TFC + TVC and TR = AR x Q, profit is equal to
questions.explanation: Profit = total revenue - total cost = (AR x Q) - TC.

questions.stem: The opportunity cost of the use of productive resources which a producer owns and so does not pay for, constitutes
questions.explanation: Costs of self-owned resources that involve no outlay are implicit costs.

questions.stem: The effect of changes in the conditions of demand on a demand schedule with the price constant is a
options: hyperbola formation by the demand curve
questions.explanation: A change in any determinant of demand other than the good's own price shifts the whole demand curve.

questions.stem: Which of the following statements is TRUE of the effect of changes in demand and supply on price?
options: A decrease in supply will lead to a fall in price and a fall in the quantity bought and sold
An increase in demand will lead to a fall in price and in the quantity bought and sold
A decrease in demand will lead to a rise in price and in the quantity bought and sold
An increase in supply will lead to a fall in price and a rise in the quantity bought and sold
questions.explanation: A rightward shift of supply lowers equilibrium price and raises equilibrium quantity.

questions.stem: In a free market economy, available resources are more efficiently allocated by complete reliance on
questions.explanation: A free market allocates resources through the price mechanism.

questions.stem: In order to maximize his profit, a businessman who faces a very elastic demand for his products is advised to
options: slightly increase the price of his products
slightly reduce the price of his products
questions.explanation: With elastic demand a small price cut raises quantity demanded more than proportionately, so total revenue rises.

questions.stem: What is the elasticity of demand for commodity X, if at a price of N25 the quantity demanded is 80 and when the price is reduced to N20 the quantity demanded is 100?
questions.explanation: %change in Qd = 20/80 = 25%; %change in P = 5/25 = 20%; elasticity = 25/20 = 1.25.

questions.topic: Methods and Tools of Economic Analysis
questions.stem: If y represents the income earned by workers in a factory, find the range of their income which satisfies the following inequality: 4y - 300 > 500
Both in the short run and in the long run, a firm maximizes its profits when
questions.explanation: The profit-maximising condition for any firm is marginal cost = marginal revenue.

questions.stem: Stocking small quantities of a variety of goods is a function of the
questions.explanation: Retailers stock small quantities of many different goods for final consumers.

questions.stem: In a joint stock company, preference shareholders are those who receive
options: high dividends when profits are high and little or nothing when profits are low
a fixed rate of dividend and have the first claim on the net profits of the company
the remaining profits after all other shareholders have been paid
dividends quarterly when others receive annually
questions.explanation: Preference shares carry a fixed dividend paid before ordinary shareholders.

questions.stem: The major reason for the survival of small shops despite competition from large business enterprises is because of
options: regularity and constant supply of commodities
their local services and longer hours of operation
they take prompt decisions and actions
questions.explanation: Small shops survive because they are close to customers and open long hours, offering convenience.

questions.stem: One of the major advantages of public enterprises is that
options: they are the largest employers of labour
they take prompt decisions and actions
questions.explanation: Public enterprises provide employment on a large scale; slow decisions and subsidies are disadvantages.

questions.stem: When public enterprises become commercialized it means that
options: the products of the enterprises are further subsidized
they are expected to operate with the primary aim of making profits
the government has decided to divest itself of such enterprises
the staff of the enterprises will be laid off
questions.explanation: Commercialisation requires a public enterprise to run on commercial, profit-making lines while still government-owned.

questions.stem: Which of the following statements are TRUE of agriculture in Nigeria? I. It provides food for the growing population II. A large proportion of the population is engaged in it III. Agricultural products are used as raw materials by the local industries IV. It serves as a source of heavy equipment to local industries
questions.explanation: Agriculture provides food, employment and industrial raw materials, but not heavy equipment.

questions.stem: In recent times, agriculture in Nigeria tends to lose its vital labour force as a result of
options: lack of an effective agricultural policy
employment opportunities in the oil sector
questions.explanation: Young people migrating from rural farming areas to towns (rural-urban drift) deprive agriculture of labour.

questions.stem: The government can influence the price of agricultural products by
options: fixing minimum prices when agricultural output is low
fixing maximum prices in years of bumper harvests
the use of buffer stocks and stabilization funds
paying all farmers producing identical crops a uniform amount of money
questions.explanation: Buffer stocks and stabilisation funds buy in surplus years and sell in shortage years to stabilise prices.

questions.stem: The crucial factors which determine the location of petroleum refineries in Nigeria are availability of raw materials and
questions.explanation: Port Harcourt and Warri refineries are near crude oil, while Kaduna's location reflected political (spread) considerations.

questions.stem: Infant industries denote industries which
options: are too young to compete in the world market
produce baby food and mothercare products
are allowed time enough to mature for recognition
questions.explanation: An infant industry is a new industry not yet able to compete with established foreign producers.

questions.stem: When compared with a labour-intensive industry, a capital-intensive industry employs more
questions.explanation: Capital-intensive production uses relatively more machinery than labour.

questions.topic: Natural Resources and the Nigerian Economy
questions.stem: The major source of Nigeria's foreign exchange is the export of
questions.explanation: Crude oil exports earn the bulk of Nigeria's foreign exchange.

questions.stem: The most important goal of OPEC is to
options: present a united front for the purpose of raising prices of crude oil
bring unity among the petroleum exporting states
ensure political stability among member states
ensure that rules on quota production are strictly followed
questions.explanation: OPEC was formed so that producers could act together to secure higher and stable crude oil prices.

questions.stem: The Central Bank's expansionary monetary policy is justified at a period
options: when the inflation rate is high and the economy is experiencing a boom
of economic depression accompanied by low capacity utilization
when trade unions are clamouring for higher wages
when the price of crude petroleum is rising
questions.explanation: Expanding money supply is appropriate in a depression with idle capacity, not during inflation or a boom.

questions.stem: A bank is said to be distressed when it
options: is unable to deal with the Central Bank
questions.explanation: A distressed bank is one in serious liquidity (and solvency) difficulty, unable to meet obligations to depositors.

questions.stem: One method through which the Central Bank can restrict the commercial banks' power of credit expansion is to
options: buy securities in the open market
reduce the rate of interest at which banks borrow from it
questions.explanation: Calling for special deposits withdraws reserves from banks and reduces their ability to lend; the other options expand credit.

questions.stem: Which of the following is mostly used to determine the cost of living?
options: prices of imported and exported commodities
questions.explanation: The consumer price index measures changes in the cost of a typical household basket.

questions.stem: The diagram explains the effect of government's imposition of an indirect tax on a good characterized by zero price elasticity of demand. The tax imposed is borne
options: equally by both the consumer and the producer
questions.explanation: With perfectly inelastic (zero elasticity) demand the price rises by the full amount of the tax, so consumers bear all of it.

questions.stem: Ajanka, a medical student entitled to an annual allowance of N6,000, decides to leave the university to take up a job where he earns N7,000 per annum. By this singular act, the national income level will
questions.explanation: The student allowance is a transfer payment not counted in national income; his N7,000 wage is a factor income, so national income rises by N7,000.

questions.stem: An increasing population might be of economic benefit to a country if
options: the female population is greater than the male population
the dependency ratio is increasing as the total population increases
a continuously higher proportion falls into the working class category
the rural and urban proportions are balanced
questions.explanation: Population growth helps when more of the people fall in the productive working-age group.

questions.stem: The demands made on each other by the agricultural and industrial sectors as the economy grows are reflected in
questions.explanation: Inter-sectoral demand (agriculture supplying industry inputs and buying its outputs) is described as backward and forward linkages.

questions.stem: Foreign exchange rate in a free market economy is determined by
questions.explanation: Under a free (floating) system the exchange rate is set by demand and supply of the currency.

questions.stem: The primary objective of all international economic organizations is to
options: ensure that third world countries get a better share of the world's resources
promote international economic co-operation for the mutual benefit of all members
enforce structural adjustment programmes on less developed countries
encourage exports from the developed to the less developed countries
questions.explanation: International economic organisations exist to promote economic co-operation for members' mutual benefit.

questions.stem: With a given level of money income, a consumer maximizes satisfaction from the consumption of goods and services when the
options: total utility derived from each good or service is increasing at an increasing rate
marginal utility derived from each good or service is increasing at the same rate
marginal utility derived per naira spent is the same for all the goods and services
total utility derived from all the goods and services is large
questions.explanation: Consumer equilibrium (equi-marginal principle): MU per naira is equal across all goods (MUa/Pa = MUb/Pb = ...).

questions.stem: Ike's scale of preference reveals that he prefers bananas to pawpaw, pawpaw to oranges and oranges to bananas. Ike's preferences are therefore
questions.explanation: Transitivity would require bananas to be preferred to oranges; preferring oranges to bananas makes the ranking inconsistent.

questions.stem: One of the features of a free market economy is that
options: resources are directed by the price mechanism
workers do not earn equal wages
the profit motive is severely constrained
decisions on the economy are taken by bureaucratic structures
questions.explanation: In a free market economy the price mechanism allocates resources.

questions.stem: One of the fundamental differences between a capitalist and a socialist economy is that while
options: the former is characterized by complete government ownership of resources, the latter is characterized by complete private ownership
in the former, prices act as signals in the allocation of resources, it is the central authority that performs this function in the latter
taxes are levied in a capitalist economy there is no taxation in a socialist economy
income and wealth are equally distributed in the socialist economy, this is not so in a capitalist economy
questions.explanation: Capitalism allocates resources through price signals; a socialist economy relies on central planning authorities.

questions.stem: When a country's population is experiencing increasing returns, that country is said to be
questions.explanation: If adding people still raises output per head (increasing returns), population is below the optimum, i.e. underpopulated.

questions.stem: In a country, if the proportion of people who are below 15 years is 45% and those above 60 years is 30%, this implies that the
options: population is growing according to Malthus theory
questions.explanation: Dependants make up 75% of the population, leaving only 25% working age, so the dependency ratio is high.

questions.stem: One of the objectives of Nigeria's current population policy is to
questions.explanation: Nigeria's 1988 National Population Policy aimed to reduce the birth/fertility rate (e.g. four children per woman).

questions.stem: Labour productivity is the ratio of
questions.explanation: Labour productivity = output per unit of labour input, i.e. output / man-hours.

questions.stem: The type of cost which has to be covered for a firm to continue production in the short run is the
questions.explanation: In the short run a firm keeps producing as long as price covers average variable cost.

questions.stem: A good is said to be inferior if its demand
questions.explanation: Inferior goods have negative income elasticity: demand falls as income rises.

If a demand curve that intersects a perfectly inelastic supply curve shifts rightward, then
options: the equilibrium price and quantity will increase
questions.explanation: With a vertical supply curve quantity cannot change, so an increase in demand raises only price.

questions.stem: If the percentage change in the income of the consumers of an industrial product is less than the resulting percentage change in the quantity demanded of the product, then the income elasticity of demand for the product is
questions.explanation: Income elasticity = %change Qd / %change income; a larger numerator gives a value greater than one.

questions.stem: A market where there are many differentiated products is called
questions.explanation: Many sellers of differentiated products characterises monopolistic competition.

questions.stem: A form of business organization which is characterized by limited authority and liability of the individual owners is the
questions.explanation: Shareholders of a joint stock company have limited liability and little day-to-day authority, which rests with the directors.

questions.stem: The suggestion that peasants in Africa have backward-bending supply curves of output implies that their response to an increase in the price of their crops will be to
questions.explanation: On the backward-bending section, a higher price is met by a lower quantity supplied.

questions.stem: What is the effect of inelastic demand for agricultural products on the income of a farmer?
options: a price rise results in its fall
a price fall results in its fall
a price fall results in its rise
a price rise leaves the income unchanged
questions.explanation: When demand is inelastic, total revenue moves in the same direction as price, so a price fall reduces farm income.

questions.stem: Plywood industries are often located near the source of
questions.explanation: Plywood uses bulky, weight-losing timber, so plants locate near forests (raw materials).

questions.stem: A firm is said to have benefited from external economies in production if it has realized
options: a more efficient management of resources
a better combination of factors of production
reduced resource costs due to operations of other firms
a higher profit level due to increased sales
questions.explanation: External economies are cost savings arising from the growth of the industry or other firms, not from the firm itself.

questions.stem: One of the dangers of the localization of industries is
questions.explanation: If a localised industry declines, workers in that area with specific skills become structurally unemployed.

questions.topic: Natural Resources and the Nigerian Economy
questions.stem: A glut in the world market for crude oil means
options: a fall in crude oil production
an excess supply of crude petroleum
a higher crude oil price offered by the buyer
a higher crude oil price demanded by the seller
questions.explanation: A glut is a situation of excess supply.

questions.stem: The main problem of the Organization of Petroleum Exporting Countries is how to
options: prevent members from violating their quota
enhance the quality of petroleum products
compete with the North Sea producers
questions.explanation: OPEC's persistent problem is members producing above their assigned quotas, undermining prices.

questions.stem: The most important attribute of money is
questions.explanation: Anything serves as money only if it is generally acceptable in exchange.

questions.stem: Which of the following is inflationary?
questions.explanation: Higher government spending raises aggregate demand and so can push up prices; the others are deflationary.

questions.stem: In commercial banking, an account from which the customer cannot withdraw money instantly is
questions.explanation: Time (fixed) deposits require notice or maturity before withdrawal.

questions.stem: Banks can create more money by
options: increasing its cash ratio with the Central Bank
lending out money from customers' deposits
questions.explanation: Credit creation occurs when banks lend part of deposits, which are redeposited and lent again.

questions.stem: Stocks and shares as well as bonds are examples of instruments used in the
questions.explanation: Shares and bonds are long-term instruments traded in the capital market.

questions.stem: The use of legally permissible means to reduce tax liabilities is known as tax
questions.explanation: Tax avoidance is legal reduction of tax; evasion is illegal.

questions.stem: The greatest proportion of government revenue in Nigeria comes from
options: income taxes on individuals and businesses
loans and grants from industrially advanced countries
questions.explanation: Most Nigerian government revenue comes from exporting crude oil, a raw material.

questions.stem: One of the factors which is likely to check the growth of public debts is
questions.explanation: A debt-equity swap converts outstanding debt into equity holdings, reducing the debt stock; rescheduling only postpones it.

The total money value of all goods and services produced in a country during a certain period is measured by using the
questions.explanation: Adding up the money value of goods and services produced is the output (product) method.

questions.stem: Privatization of government-owned companies means the
options: relinquishing of government's equity participation to private individuals
joint participation of government and private individuals
commercialization and deregulation of the economy
questions.explanation: Privatisation transfers government's ownership (equity) in enterprises to private investors.

questions.stem: The major determinant of the total volume of output in an economy is the
questions.explanation: In Keynesian analysis, aggregate (total) expenditure determines the level of output and income.

questions.stem: Which of the following classes of goods accounts for the largest proportion of Nigeria's imports?
questions.explanation: Machinery and transport equipment have long been the largest category of Nigeria's imports.

questions.stem: Counter trading is an international arrangement whereby
options: goods and services are exchanged in a manner similar to barter
goods and services are sold on the counter
crude oil is sold to a foreign country
goods are shipped to countries on which the United Nations has placed a trade embargo
questions.explanation: Counter trade is the exchange of goods for goods between countries, a form of barter.

questions.stem: In recent years, Nigeria's balance of payments has continued to register a deficit due to I. Increased government overseas spending II. Increasing prices of exports III. Rising import prices IV. More payments to overseas investors
questions.explanation: Overseas spending, dearer imports and payments to foreign investors worsen the balance; rising export prices would improve it.

questions.stem: The organization which provides credits to help countries achieve short-term balance in their balance of payments is the
options: Economic Community of West African States
International Bank for Reconstruction and Development
questions.explanation: The IMF gives short-term credit for balance of payments problems; the World Bank (IBRD) finances long-term development.

questions.stem: Units of consumption of commodity X - Marginal utility (units): 1 - 100; 2 - 80; 3 - 50; 4 - 20. From the table above, the total utility for the individual who consumes 3 units of commodity X is
questions.explanation: Total utility = sum of marginal utilities = 100 + 80 + 50 = 230 units.

questions.topic: Natural Resources and the Nigerian Economy
questions.stem: One of the economic problems of Nigeria today arises from
options: the overutilization of human and natural resources
the underutilization of human and natural resources
questions.explanation: Nigeria has abundant human and natural resources that are under-utilised (unemployment, untapped minerals).

questions.stem: In certain circumstances, a centrally planned economy adopts the rationing system because of
options: the scarcity of goods and services in the market
the need for equitable distribution of goods and services
questions.explanation: Rationing is used in a planned economy when goods are scarce and prices are not allowed to clear the market.

questions.stem: Given that B = Births, X = Emigrants, D = Deaths, M = Immigrants. The population of a country over a period of time will rise if
questions.explanation: With natural increase zero (B = D), population rises only if immigrants exceed emigrants (M > X).

questions.stem: The short-run period in production is defined as a period when
options: there is at least one fixed factor
all costs of production must be covered
questions.explanation: The short run is the period in which at least one factor input is fixed.

questions.stem: Specialization often improves economic performance because it
options: permits exploitation of economies of scale
is based on the law of variable proportions
allocates resources according to absolute advantage
questions.explanation: Specialisation allows large-scale production and so the exploitation of economies of scale.

questions.stem: Which of the following statements best describes the relationship between average product and marginal product?
options: Marginal product and average product curves rise and fall together
Marginal product equals average product at the minimum point of the latter
Average product curve will rise as long as marginal product is greater than average product
Marginal product equals average product at the maximum point of the former
questions.explanation: When MP exceeds AP it pulls AP up; MP cuts AP at AP's maximum.

questions.stem: Total output (units) - Fixed cost (N) - Variable cost (N): 100 - 100 - 100; 120 - 100 - 110; 160 - 100 - 120; 200 - 100 - 140; 240 - 100 - 160. The average total cost when output is 200 units in the table above is
When a firm is reaping economies of large-scale production, it experiences a fall in its
questions.explanation: Economies of scale are shown by a falling long-run average cost curve.

questions.stem: If an increase in the price of a commodity leads to an increase in total revenue, then it means that the demand for this commodity is
questions.explanation: When demand is inelastic, price and total revenue move in the same direction.

questions.stem: Given that the elasticity of demand for a commodity is 2.5, the percentage change in the quantity demanded as a result of a 10 percent change in its price is
questions.explanation: %change in Qd = elasticity x %change in price = 2.5 x 10 = 25%.

questions.stem: The producer in a perfectly competitive market is faced with a demand curve whose elasticity is
questions.explanation: A perfectly competitive firm faces a horizontal (perfectly elastic) demand curve.

questions.stem: Unlike the retailer, the wholesaler provides
options: useful information to the manufacturer about consumers' taste
after sales service to the consumer
useful information to the customers on the benefits and uses of the product
useful information about market trends and finance to the manufacturer
questions.explanation: The wholesaler deals directly with manufacturers, financing them by bulk purchase and advising them on market trends.

questions.stem: Liquidation of a limited liability company implies that the
options: company may not pay its debt
debts of the company can only be paid from its own assets
debts of the company are paid from both business and private funds of the owners
debts of the company must be paid from public funds only
questions.explanation: With limited liability, creditors are paid only from the company's assets, not the owners' private property.

questions.stem: One form of business organization which is not motivated solely by the profit objective is the
questions.explanation: Co-operative societies exist mainly to serve members' welfare rather than to maximise profit.

questions.stem: Which of the following can have their shares quoted on the stock exchange?
questions.explanation: Only public limited companies can have their shares listed and traded on the stock exchange.

questions.stem: The sector that employs the largest proportion of the active labour force in Nigeria is the
questions.explanation: Agriculture employs most of Nigeria's working population.

questions.stem: A factor that influences the location of a firm near its market is the
options: high cost of transporting finished goods
questions.explanation: Where finished products are costly to transport (bulky or perishable), firms locate near their markets.

questions.stem: In many developing countries, infrastructural problem is acute due to the shortage of
options: supporting services that encourage economic activities
questions.explanation: Infrastructure consists of supporting services (roads, power, water, communication) that facilitate economic activity.

questions.stem: Export-promotion policy is primarily concerned with the
options: processing of raw materials to increase their value
making of international routes safe for export commodities
reduction in the number of imported items
encouragement of the production of export commodities
questions.explanation: Export promotion encourages production of goods for export.

questions.topic: Natural Resources and the Nigerian Economy
questions.stem: The petroleum industry in Nigeria is
options: the sole source of the nation's revenue
the oldest industry in the country
a factor in the decline in the nation's foreign reserves
questions.explanation: Petroleum provides most of government revenue and export earnings, making it the mainstay of the economy.

questions.topic: Natural Resources and the Nigerian Economy
questions.stem: Crude petroleum is a good example of a
questions.explanation: Crude oil is non-renewable and is depleted as it is extracted, i.e. a wasting asset.

questions.stem: One of the techniques of monetary control used by the Central Bank of Nigeria is
questions.explanation: Selective credit control is a monetary policy instrument; budget deficit is fiscal policy.

questions.stem: Which of the following is true about the value of money?
options: It varies inversely with the price level
It varies directly with the price level
It depreciates in the period of deflation
It is not affected by the price level
questions.explanation: When prices rise, a unit of money buys less, so value of money and price level move inversely.

questions.stem: If the reserve requirement for commercial banking in Nigeria were 30%, a commercial bank which receives an initial cash deposit of N3,000 is in a position to lend out
questions.explanation: Required reserve = 30% x 3,000 = N900; excess reserve available for lending = 3,000 - 900 = N2,100.

questions.stem: An issue of bank-notes not backed by gold but by government securities is known as
questions.explanation: Currency backed by government securities rather than gold is the fiduciary issue.

questions.stem: A rise in the market price of fixed interest securities is an indication that the
options: market rate of interest has risen
market rate of interest has fallen
questions.explanation: Prices of fixed-interest securities move inversely with the market rate of interest.

questions.stem: An increase in government expenditure will lead to
options: an increase in the level of aggregate demand
an increase in total tax revenue
questions.explanation: Government expenditure is a component of aggregate demand, so raising it increases aggregate demand.

questions.stem: When an indirect tax is levied on the producer of a good, the burden on the consumer will depend largely on the
options: elasticity of demand for the good
proportion of the consumer's income spent on the goods
elasticity of demand and supply of the commodity
availability of substitutes for the commodity
questions.explanation: Tax incidence is shared according to the relative elasticities of demand and supply.

questions.stem: If a government wants to reduce the level of inflation, it will
questions.explanation: A budget surplus withdraws more from the economy through taxes than it injects, reducing aggregate demand.

questions.stem: If a country's national income increased from N1,000 billion to N1,100 billion over a period of 2 years, what was the average annual rate of growth of national income over the period?
questions.explanation: Total growth = 100/1,000 = 10% over 2 years, an average of about 5% a year.

questions.stem: A fall in the marginal propensity to save will lead to
questions.explanation: A lower MPS raises the multiplier (1/MPS) and consumption, increasing national income.

questions.stem: Which of the following is a transfer payment?
options: Gift to a motherless babies' home
questions.explanation: A gift is a payment for which no good or service is rendered in return, i.e. a transfer payment.

questions.stem: The major objective of economic growth is to
options: redistribute income and other benefits of growth
equalize opportunities for education and employment
increase the aggregate expenditure on goods and services
increase the real per capita income
questions.explanation: Economic growth aims at a sustained rise in real output and income per head.

questions.stem: Economically underdeveloped countries are characterized by
options: high rate of population growth and low rate of economic growth
high rate of economic growth and low rate of population growth
high rate of population growth and high rate of economic growth
low rate of population growth and low rate of economic growth
questions.explanation: Less developed countries typically have rapid population growth and slow economic growth.

questions.stem: One of the major consequences of urban-biased development programmes in Nigeria is that they
options: transformed rural areas into urban centres
increased the level of specialized manpower in the cities
questions.explanation: Concentrating amenities and jobs in towns pulls people from rural areas, causing rural-urban migration.

questions.stem: Development plans have not been successful in some developing countries largely because of
options: shortage of skilled labour and experts
questions.explanation: Plan implementation is frequently hampered by a shortage of skilled manpower and experts.

questions.stem: The balance of visible trade is the difference between the value of
options: exchange rate of local and foreign currencies
questions.explanation: Visible trade concerns physical goods; the balance of trade = value of goods exported minus goods imported.

questions.stem: If a country has a balance of payments surplus on current account, this means that
options: the total invisible export is greater than invisible import
the value of goods exported must be greater than the value of goods imported
there must be a positive balance on capital account
the aggregate of the balance of trade and the invisible balance must be positive
questions.explanation: The current account combines visible (trade) and invisible balances; a surplus means their sum is positive.

questions.stem: If a country operates a freely floating exchange rate system, and suffers a balance of payments deficit, the deficit can be eliminated through
options: a rise in the external value of its currency
a fall in the external value of its currency
an increase in the volume of imports
the consumption of more foreign goods
questions.explanation: A deficit causes the currency to depreciate, making exports cheaper and imports dearer, which corrects the deficit.

questions.stem: The Economic Commission for Africa was set up by the
questions.explanation: The ECA (1958) is one of the regional commissions of the United Nations.

questions.topic: Methods and Tools of Economic Analysis
questions.stem: In a firm three employees earn N5,500 each, four earn N3,300 each, two earn N5,000 each and one earns N7,000. The mean income of the employees is
Abubakar has the choice of buying either a house or a Mercedes Benz car for N1.5m plus N0.5m running cost. If he decides to buy the Mercedes Benz car, his opportunity cost is
questions.explanation: Opportunity cost is the alternative forgone - the house - not a money sum.

questions.stem: The shape of a production possibility frontier is determined by the
options: diminishing returns to a fixed factor
increasing returns to a variable factor
questions.explanation: The PPF is concave to the origin because of increasing opportunity (relative) costs as resources are shifted.

questions.stem: Normative economics deals with
options: what is and not what should be
questions.explanation: Normative economics concerns what ought to be, i.e. value judgements; positive economics deals with what is.

questions.stem: The determinants of elasticity include
options: price, time and availability of alternatives
questions.explanation: Elasticity depends on factors such as time period and availability of substitutes; price itself is not a determinant of elasticity.

questions.stem: Period 1: family income N1,000, expenditure on clothing N100. Period 2: family income N1,500, expenditure on clothing N200. From the table, the income elasticity of clothing is
questions.explanation: %change in clothing = 100/100 = 100%; %change in income = 500/1,000 = 50%; income elasticity = 100/50 = 2.0.

questions.stem: A capitalist economy is one characterized by the
options: private ownership of factors of production
ownership of factors of production by rich members of the society
use of capital and labour in fixed proportions during production
use of capital intensive methods of production
questions.explanation: Capitalism is defined by private ownership of the means of production.

questions.stem: In a planned economy, what shall be produced is determined primarily by
questions.explanation: In a centrally planned economy the state/planning authority decides what to produce.

questions.stem: A utility maximizing household will allocate its expenditure so that
options: more naira is spent on commodities with the highest utility
less naira is spent on commodities with the lowest utility
the utility of the last naira spent on each commodity is equal
the amount spent on each commodity is equal
questions.explanation: Equi-marginal principle: utility is maximised when the marginal utility per last naira is equal across goods.

questions.stem: The downward sloping part of the long-run average cost curve of a firm may be attributable to
questions.explanation: LRAC falls when the firm enjoys increasing returns (economies) of scale.

questions.stem: The main function of price in the economic system is to
options: allocate scarce resources among competing uses
ensure equitable distribution of income and wealth
determine the demand for and the supply of goods and services
remove all the constraints on production of goods and services
questions.explanation: Prices signal relative scarcity and so allocate scarce resources among competing uses.

questions.stem: Sector - No. of people: I. Agriculture, forestry and fishing 10,050; II. Mining and quarrying 1,500; III. Transport and communication 2,000,000; IV. Manufacturing 1,750,000; V. Basic construction 750,000; VI. Distributive 3,000,000; VII. Administration 1,250,000. Calculate the total number of people engaged in tertiary production from the data above.
questions.explanation: Tertiary = transport and communication + distributive + administration = 2,000,000 + 3,000,000 + 1,250,000 = 6,250,000.

questions.stem: One of the characteristics of an imperfect market is the
options: large number of buyers and sellers in the market
awareness of market conditions by buyers
questions.explanation: Differentiated (heterogeneous) products mark an imperfect market; homogeneous products, many buyers/sellers and perfect knowledge describe perfect competition.

questions.stem: A characteristic of the average fixed cost is that it
options: rises and falls faster than the marginal cost
is U-shaped and intersects the price axis
is always higher than the average variable cost
falls continuously but is never equal to zero
questions.explanation: AFC = TFC/Q falls continuously as output rises but never reaches zero (a rectangular hyperbola).

questions.stem: In perfect competition, every firm is a price
questions.explanation: A perfectly competitive firm cannot influence market price; it is a price taker.

questions.stem: Given that the total fixed cost is N1,000, total variable cost N2,500 and the output 100 units, find the average total cost of producing one unit.
Which of the following falls continuously as output expands?
questions.explanation: AFC falls continuously as a fixed total is spread over more units; MC, AVC and AC are U-shaped.

questions.stem: A major obstacle to rapid agricultural development in Nigeria is the
options: inability of farmers to adopt modern technology
introduction of the Green Revolution programme
questions.explanation: Most Nigerian farmers still lack the means and knowledge to adopt modern techniques, hampering agricultural growth.

questions.stem: The land tenure system in Nigeria impedes agricultural production because
options: land fragmentation makes possible easy access to land ownership
it discourages specialization of factors of production
it limits opportunity for mass production of agricultural goods
small landholders generally do not get enough fertilizers to use
questions.explanation: Communal/inheritance tenure fragments land into small plots, preventing large-scale (mass) farming.

questions.stem: The primary objective of establishing the Export Processing Zone is to
options: encourage the production and processing of export commodities
erect structures that will facilitate the processing of imported raw materials
erect economic structures near the port
questions.explanation: Export Processing Zones offer incentives to firms that produce and process goods for export.

questions.topic: Natural Resources and the Nigerian Economy
questions.stem: The first petroleum exploring company to discover crude petroleum in Nigeria was
questions.explanation: Shell-BP discovered oil in commercial quantity at Oloibiri in 1956.

questions.stem: Concentrating industries in one place is advantageous because there are gains in terms of
questions.explanation: Localisation of industry yields external economies (shared infrastructure, skilled labour, ancillary firms).

questions.stem: Import substitution industrialization refers to
options: the concentration of industries for even development
setting up of industries for regional development
a situation in which local industries are set up to produce goods formerly imported
the banning of imports which are substitutes for domestically produced goods
questions.explanation: Import substitution means producing locally goods that were previously imported.

questions.topic: Factors of Production and their Theories
questions.stem: An entrepreneur will continue to employ labour up to a point where
options: wages are equal to marginal product of labour
marginal product of labour is equal to zero
questions.explanation: By marginal productivity theory, labour is hired until the wage equals the (value of the) marginal product of labour.

questions.stem: Optimum population is defined as the level of population at which
options: population is neither increasing nor decreasing
marginal efficiency of population is maximized
questions.explanation: Optimum population is the size that, with given resources and technology, maximises output (income) per head.

questions.topic: Factors of Production and their Theories
questions.stem: When a worker earns more than the wage just sufficient to keep him in his job the excess income is called
questions.explanation: Earnings above transfer earnings are economic rent.

questions.stem: Items (N million): 1. Wages 9,000; 2. Salaries 7,000; 3. Government pensions 1,500; 4. Unemployment pay and other social benefits 1,000; 5. Rent and interest 1,500; 6. Profits 1,500. From the table above calculate the national income.
questions.explanation: Exclude transfer payments (pensions, unemployment benefits): 9,000 + 7,000 + 1,500 + 1,500 = N19,000m.

questions.stem: Non-bank financial intermediaries do not
questions.explanation: Only commercial banks accept demand (current account) deposits withdrawable by cheque.

questions.stem: Inflation which is caused mainly by increases in the prices of factors of production is described as
questions.explanation: Rising input/factor costs push up prices: cost-push inflation.

questions.stem: The relationship between the value of money and the price level is
questions.explanation: As the price level rises the purchasing power (value) of money falls.

questions.stem: People hold money for
questions.explanation: Keynes's motives for holding money are transactions, precautionary and speculative.

questions.stem: If high unemployment goes hand in hand with rising prices the situation created is
questions.explanation: Stagflation is the coexistence of stagnation (high unemployment) and inflation.

questions.stem: Fiscal policy involves changes in
questions.explanation: Fiscal policy is the use of government taxation (revenue) and spending.

questions.stem: Economic development may be defined as economic growth
questions.explanation: Development is growth accompanied by structural and welfare changes such as a fairer distribution of income and wealth.

questions.stem: The price of a good will not be affected by the imposition of a sales tax on it if the
questions.explanation: With perfectly elastic demand, sellers cannot raise the price and must absorb the whole tax.

questions.stem: A free trade area emerges when
options: traders from one part of the country can move freely to other parts
customs regulations are harmonized among countries
a group of countries decide to remove restrictions on imports from one another
questions.explanation: In a free trade area member countries abolish trade barriers among themselves while keeping their own external tariffs.

questions.stem: Devaluation helps in checking adverse balance of payments if the
questions.explanation: Devaluation makes imports dearer; if import demand is elastic, import spending falls substantially, improving the balance.

questions.stem: Gains from trade depend on
questions.explanation: By Ricardo's principle, mutual gains from trade arise from comparative advantage.

questions.stem: Favourable terms of trade is important to a country because it facilitates
options: economic prosperity for importers and exporters
export of hard currency by the government
import of hard currency by the government
questions.explanation: Favourable terms of trade mean each unit of exports buys more imports, raising national welfare.

questions.stem: The most acceptable economic measure for trade protection is to
questions.explanation: The infant-industry argument is the most widely accepted economic case for protection.

questions.stem: Economics can be defined as
options: reduction in spending in the face of competing alternatives
allocation of resources to alternative uses
economic behaviour of small units like the household and the firm
the study of economic aggregates like inflation and national income
questions.explanation: Economics studies how scarce resources are allocated among alternative uses; C and D describe only micro- and macroeconomics.

questions.stem:
I. What and how much will be produced?
II. How will it be produced?
III. For whom will it be produced?
IV. How much will be exported and consumed?
From the above, identify the combination of basic resource allocation questions in economic analysis.
questions.explanation: The basic economic questions every society answers are what (and how much), how, and for whom to produce.

questions.stem: In a capitalist economy, the economic problem of what goods to produce is decided mainly by
questions.explanation: In a free-market (capitalist) economy the price mechanism, i.e. relative prices, signals what goods should be produced.

questions.stem: Which of the following is an example of derived demand?
questions.explanation: Labour is demanded not for itself but for the goods and services it helps to produce, so its demand is derived.

questions.stem:
When commodity X sold for N25 per unit, 50 units of commodity Y were purchased. With an increase in the price of commodity X to N50 per unit, the demand for commodity Y fell to 20 units.
Determine the cross elasticity of demand.
questions.explanation: %change in Qy = (20-50)/50 = -60%; %change in Px = (50-25)/25 = +100%; cross elasticity = -60/100 = -0.6.

questions.stem:
When commodity X sold for N25 per unit, 50 units of commodity Y were purchased. With an increase in the price of commodity X to N50 per unit, the demand for commodity Y fell to 20 units.
The two commodities can be classified as
questions.explanation: A rise in the price of X reduced the demand for Y, giving a negative cross elasticity, which indicates complements.

questions.stem: A central argument of cardinal utility is that utility is
questions.explanation: Cardinal utility theory assumes satisfaction can be measured in units (utils); ordinal theory only ranks it.

questions.stem: In a free market system, trading can only take place when the
options: price of a commodity tends to attract consumers
questions.explanation: In a free market, transactions clear at the equilibrium price where the quantities buyers and sellers wish to trade are equal.

questions.stem: The condition for equilibrium price and quantity under perfect competition is
questions.explanation: A perfectly competitive firm is in equilibrium where MC = MR, and since MR = AR = P, MC = AR = P.

questions.stem: External diseconomies of scale result from excessive growth of
questions.explanation: External (dis)economies arise from the growth of the whole industry, e.g. congestion and rising input prices, not from the firm itself.

If a total cost curve is plotted, marginal cost can be illustrated by the
options: slope of the tangent to the curve at any given output
U-shaped curve cutting the total cost curve at its lowest point
straight line from the origin to the midpoint of the curve
straight line cutting the curve at its highest point
questions.explanation: Marginal cost is the rate of change of total cost, i.e. the slope of the tangent to the TC curve at each output.

questions.stem: The short-run equilibrium in a perfectly competitive market requires that
options: marginal cost be equal to total revenue
marginal cost and marginal revenue be equal
costs are mutually determined by buyers and sellers
the marginal cost curve cuts the total cost curve
questions.explanation: Any profit-maximising firm, including a perfect competitor in the short run, produces where MC = MR.

questions.stem: At the point where marginal revenue of a monopolist is equal to zero, its total revenue will be
questions.explanation: TR rises while MR is positive and falls when MR is negative, so TR is at its maximum where MR = 0.

questions.stem: A distinguishing characteristic of cooperative societies is that voting power depends on the
questions.explanation: Cooperatives operate on "one member, one vote" regardless of shares held, so members vote as equals.

questions.stem: The concept of privatization presupposes
questions.explanation: Privatization rests on the premise that private ownership will run enterprises more efficiently than the state.

questions.stem: One problem in the marketing of agricultural products in Nigeria is
options: the seasonal nature of the commodities
questions.explanation: Inadequate storage facilities cause wastage of perishable produce and force farmers to sell at low prices at harvest.

questions.stem: Increased output will cause farmers' revenue to decrease when market demand is
questions.explanation: With inelastic demand, the larger output lowers price proportionately more than quantity rises, so total revenue falls.

questions.stem: A primary industry is concerned with
options: extraction of resources in their raw state
the operation of small scale enterprises
the economic activities of primary producers
clearing and cultivation of land only
questions.explanation: Primary industries (farming, fishing, mining, forestry) extract natural resources in their raw state.

questions.stem: The slow pace of industrial growth in Nigeria can be attributed to
questions.explanation: Poor power supply, roads and other infrastructure raise costs and are a major constraint on Nigerian industrial growth.

questions.topic: Natural Resources and the Nigerian Economy
questions.stem: The Nigerian economy is monocultural because government revenue is derived mainly from
questions.explanation: Nigeria depends on a single product, crude oil, for most of its government revenue and export earnings.

questions.stem: As a producers' association, the OPEC expects its members to maintain production where marginal cost is
questions.explanation: OPEC acts as a cartel restricting output like a monopolist, so production is held where price exceeds marginal cost.

questions.stem: A well conducted census is important for
questions.explanation: Accurate census figures on population size and structure are needed for good economic planning.

questions.stem: The age distribution of a country's population determines the
options: ratio of the dependent to the working group
total age of all working class adults
questions.explanation: Age structure shows how many people are of working age versus dependants (young and old), i.e. the dependency ratio.

questions.topic: Factors of Production and their Theories
questions.stem: Firms continue to employ workers until the wage rate equals the
options: sum of marginal revenue and average revenue of labour
questions.explanation: By marginal productivity theory, a firm hires labour up to the point where the wage equals the marginal revenue product of labour.

questions.stem: A major effect of a long distribution chain is
questions.explanation: Each middleman in a long chain adds a profit margin, raising the final retail price.

questions.stem: The major function of the wholesaler to his customers is
questions.explanation: Wholesalers buy in bulk from producers and break it into smaller quantities for retailers, their customers.

questions.stem: Which of the following is used for measuring national income?
questions.explanation: National income is measured by the income, output (product) and expenditure approaches.

questions.stem: Exclusions that make Gross National Product a poor measure of welfare are
questions.explanation: Unpaid services such as housewives' work add to welfare but are excluded from GNP because they are not marketed.

questions.stem: An increase in money supply, other things being equal, will
questions.explanation: With money demand unchanged, a larger money supply lowers the price of money, the rate of interest.

questions.stem: A persistent rise in the general level of prices implies
options: a steady fall in the purchasing power of money
that the higher the price level, the more the value of money
questions.explanation: Inflation, a persistent rise in the general price level, steadily erodes what a unit of money can buy.

questions.stem: Two principal ways by which banks can lend money to their customers are through
questions.explanation: Commercial banks lend to customers mainly through loans and overdrafts.

questions.stem: A capital market differs from the money market in that in the former
options: the percentage of interest charged is more
questions.explanation: The capital market deals in long-term funds, while the money market deals in short-term funds.

questions.stem: An aspect of taxation that involves normative economics is the
questions.explanation: Whether a tax is fair is a value judgement, which is the domain of normative economics.

questions.stem: Public debt is composed of
options: internal debts and World Bank loans
money owed to local and foreign contractors
loans granted by IMF and ADB
questions.explanation: Public (national) debt is the total of what government owes at home (internal) and abroad (external).

questions.stem: A country's import price index by 1995 was 50 and her index of export price was 70. Calculate the terms of trade.
questions.explanation: Terms of trade = (export price index / import price index) x 100 = 70/50 x 100 = 140%.

questions.stem: If the United Kingdom buys gold for £60 an ounce and Nigeria buys the same ounce for N500, what will be United Kingdom's exchange rate with Nigeria?
questions.explanation: By purchasing power parity, £60 = N500, so N1 = 60/500 = £0.12.

questions.stem: Being a member of the OPEC, Nigeria is in a favourable position to
options: reap the benefit of a cartel
questions.explanation: OPEC is a cartel; members gain from collectively restricting output to keep oil prices high.

questions.stem: If the price elasticity of demand for a good is 0.43, an increase in the price of the good will result in
questions.explanation: Demand is inelastic (0.43 < 1), so a price rise reduces quantity proportionately less and total revenue rises: a net gain.

questions.stem: In a free market economy the price system allocates resources
questions.explanation: Prices signal where resources earn the most, so the price system moves resources to their best alternative uses.

questions.stem: At consumer equilibrium, the slope of the indifference curve is
options: half the slope of the budget constraint line
equal to the slope of the budget constraint line
greater than the slope of the budget constraint line
less than the slope of the budget constraint line
questions.explanation: Equilibrium is where the budget line is tangent to the highest indifference curve, so their slopes are equal (MRS = price ratio).

questions.stem: For a supply curve, an increase in the price of a commodity will result in
options: a decrease in the quantity supplied
an increase in the quantity supplied
questions.explanation: A change in the commodity's own price causes a movement along the supply curve: a higher price raises quantity supplied.

questions.stem: A normal good with close substitutes is likely to have price elasticity of demand
questions.explanation: Close substitutes let consumers switch easily when price rises, making demand elastic (greater than 1).

questions.topic: Methods and Tools of Economic Analysis
questions.stem: Economics is regarded as a social science because it
options: adopts the scientific method in production
adopts the scientific method in the study of human behaviour
questions.explanation: Economics applies scientific method (observation, hypothesis, testing) to human behaviour, making it a social science.

questions.stem: A change in supply is best described as a
options: shift of the supply curve to the left or to the right
shift of the supply curve to the left
shift of the supply curve to the right
questions.explanation: A change in supply (caused by non-price factors) shifts the whole curve either left or right.

questions.topic: Methods and Tools of Economic Analysis
questions.stem: When a generalization is made based on observed facts, it is known as
questions.explanation: Induction moves from observed particular facts to general conclusions.

questions.stem: A major problem facing all economies is how to
options: transform from a developing to a developed economy
questions.explanation: Scarcity makes the allocation of limited resources the basic economic problem of every economy.

questions.stem: A vertical supply curve indicates that
options: the quantity supplied is responsive to price
the same fixed quantity will be supplied no matter the price
an increase in price will result in an increase in the quantity supplied
there is a fixed price for the commodity below which no supply will be made
questions.explanation: A vertical supply curve is perfectly inelastic: quantity supplied does not change with price.

questions.stem: In a demand curve, the relationship between price and quantity is
questions.explanation: By the law of demand, quantity demanded falls as price rises, an inverse relationship.

questions.stem: A consumer's scale of preference is an arrangement of his
options: scarce resources in order of importance
sources of income and their importance
requirement and how to satisfy them
questions.explanation: A scale of preference lists a person's wants/needs in order of priority.

questions.stem: A firm's shut-down point is reached when the average revenue fails to cover the
questions.explanation: In the short run a firm shuts down if price (AR) cannot cover average variable cost.

questions.stem: Internal economies of scale are expected to bring about
options: an increase in short-run average cost
an increase in long-run average cost
a decrease in long-run average cost
a decrease in short-run average cost
questions.explanation: Internal economies of scale lower the firm's long-run average cost as its scale of output grows.

questions.stem: In the long run a monopolist maximizes his profit when the marginal cost equals
questions.explanation: Every profit maximiser, including a monopolist, produces where MC = MR.

questions.stem: The long run is a period during which a firm
options: sells input to purchase fixed asset
sources all its inputs from within
questions.explanation: In the long run all factors are variable.

questions.stem: An important feature of perfect competition is that
options: the movement of goods and services is restricted
there is adequate knowledge of existing prices
individual economic units can influence prices
questions.explanation: Perfect competition assumes perfect knowledge of market prices by buyers and sellers.

questions.stem: If government fixes price below the equilibrium price, what effect will it have on demand?
options: Quantity demanded and supplied will be equal.
Quantity supplied will be greater than quantity demanded.
questions.explanation: A maximum price below equilibrium makes the good cheaper, so quantity demanded rises (creating a shortage).

questions.stem: An imperfect market exists where
options: there is perfect information among the few buyers and sellers
both buyers and sellers have free entry into and free exit from the market
the location of some sellers gives them an advantage over others
questions.explanation: Locational advantages give some sellers market power, an imperfection; the other options are features of perfect markets.

questions.stem: A production function relates
questions.explanation: A production function expresses output as a function of the inputs used.
